classes.name: Berserker
classes.flavor:
The Berserker is destruction. He knows not fatigue nor caution—both driven away in a relentless fury. Even death fears to take a Berserker before his battle Rage is satiated. Once a Berserker has begun to fight, he only grows stronger, fueled by battle-lust and unending Rage.

The deadliest among them is not the well-rested, but those who are pushed to the brink through combat. It matters not what a Berserker wields, be it axe or sword; flesh will be hewn from bone and heads from shoulders. Many have caved under the Berserker’s primal might—sword and spell are but straw in the wake of unbridled RAGE.
highlights: Become a raging, damage-dealing machine. Greet death as an old friend and keep on fighting!
Deal out incredible amounts of brutality: the longer a fight goes on, the more your Rage intensifies.
Use your Savage Arsenal. Choose abilities to crush your foes and laugh in the face of death!

faq.q: Fury Dice
faq.a: These are NOT expended when making an attack. You keep accumulating them as your fury grows, they are only lost when your Rage ends (at the end of combat or when you gain the Dying condition) or when you expend them to use an ability like “That all you got?!”

faq.q: Intensifying Fury
faq.a: You can still Rage 1/turn with this feature. That is: you can still spend an action to Rage and roll an additional Fury Die.

faq.q: Enduring Rage
faq.a:
You cannot Rage again on a turn you’ve triggered this ability since Rage is limited to 1/turn. “Free” means only that you don’t have to use an action or other resources to do it.

This ability does stack with Intensifying Fury since both happen “at the beginning of your turn” (example: when you first gain the Dying condition your Rage ends and you lose all your Fury Dice; then at the beginning of your turn, you Rage for free from Enduring Rage; then roll an additional Fury Die for free from Intensifying Fury).

faq.q: Path of the Mountainheart: Unbreakable
faq.a: This applies to ANY condition listed in the Core Rules or any other special condition applied by monsters or environmental effects. If you negate the Dying condition you drop to 1 HP instead.

classes.flavor:
An “empire” isn’t an EMPIRE until they have their own academy of command: Famed schools where these supremely capable soldiers are trained in battlefield tactics and leadership.

Among the most skilled soldiers in the world, Commanders are masters of every weapon and form of close combat. A small cohort of soldiers led by a trained Commander is more feared than innumerable legions without one.

Exert mastery over all weapon types, wielding them with deadly efficiency—ensuring victory against any foe.
Lead your party to triumph through cunning strategy, tactical prowess, and decisive action.

subclasses.intro:
Arcane Command. Your focus on the arcane causes you to lose access to Weapon Mastery and Combat Tactics, but you now gain INT mana when you roll Initiative (this mana is lost if unspent when combat ends). Whenever you could choose a Combat Tactic or Weapon Mastery, instead choose another Commander’s Order or a tier 1 (or lower) spell from any spell school. Your Commander’s Orders are also empowered with magical power:
• Face Me! (Glimmering Decree). Free Reaction (whenever an enemy crits or attacks a Dying ally): That enemy takes STR d8 radiant damage (ignoring armor), is pulled up to 4 spaces toward you, and is Taunted by you until you drop to 0 HP.
• Move it! Move it! (Borne upon the Wind). When you roll Initiative, you may give yourself and an ally advantage on the roll, +3 Speed, and the ability to fly for 1 round. Then, you both can also move for free.
• Hold the Line! (Crystalline Armor). (1/encounter) Reaction (when an ally drops to 0 HP): Command them to continue the fight! Set their HP to 3× your LVL. Additionally, they gain that many temp HP. Enemies who reduce this temp HP in melee have their Speed halved until the end of their next turn.
• Reposition! (Flashstep). Action: Command 1 ally to move up to their Speed (or 2 allies up to half their Speed) for free; you may exchange places with one of them. You may use this as a reaction on an ally’s turn.
• I Can Do This ALL DAY! (Rising Phoenix). (1/encounter) Reaction (when you would drop to 0 HP): You may expend any number of Hit Dice, set your HP to the sum rolled instead, and deal that much fire damage to each enemy within Reach 2 of you. They gain the Smoldering condition.
• Commanding Presence (Withering Presence). Creatures you Command suffer necrotic damage equal to the max value of your Combat Die (ignoring armor) and are considered undead for 1 round.

classes.name: Hunter
classes.tagline: A master of the wild, adept at ranged attacks and high burst damage up close.
classes.flavor:
Long before the first stones of the grand kingdoms had been laid, there was The Wild. We Hunters called groves and fields home, just as the elk and boar still do. We have trained our minds and hearts as much as we have trained with bows. For there is great danger in becoming a Hunter: the intoxicating Thrill of the Hunt that washes over your body when stalking prey.

Be warned—do not let it settle into your heart. For no true Hunter takes without recognizing what they have first been given: a soul, a meal, warmth, all at a cost—a life. And that should not be taken lightly. Wherever you roam, be it city or glade, mountain or valley, as long as The Wild is tenderly tucked into the depths of your heart, you will always be a Hunter.

May your arrows strike true and your bowstrings never break!
highlights: As an expert survivalist, you mark your prey, becoming a relentless tracker in pursuit.
Whether you’re raining arrows from a distance or closing in for a personal takedown, your prey won’t escape.
Harness the Thrill of the Hunt to outwit your targets—set decoys, spring traps, and strike with lethal efficiency.

No Stats or Actions to Track! Your companion’s HP and movement are abstracted; it knows where it is most needed without being told—whether defending you or attacking your Quarry. It is smart enough, and you are caring enough, to make sure it is never put in mortal danger.

Extra Abilities? At the GM’s discretion, your companion can also do anything the base animal can do: fly, sniff out scents, be used as a mount, etc. Even more complex actions like Grapple or Help may be doable if it makes sense (you’ll need to spend 1 action to command it though—it won’t do it on its own).

faq.q: How many TotH charges can I hold?
faq.a: No limit, but they do expire at the end of combat, so use them up!

faq.q: Does a melee crit give me a charge?
faq.a: Yes. A crit is also a hit.

faq.q: Do I get a TotH charge when anyone kills my Quarry?
faq.a: Yes. But if you kill it, you may get an additional charge for hitting/critting them.

faq.q: Do abilities such as Hail of Arrows and Pinning Shot also deal damage?
faq.a: Yes, they deal damage as normal.

faq.q: What is Half Range?
faq.a: Half of your weapon’s Range (e.g., a Longbow’s normal Range is 16, Half Range would be 8).

faq.q: Final Takedown: they crit you back. Can it be Defended or Interposed against?
faq.a: Yes. Treat it as a normal attack but change their Primary Die to its max.

faq.q: Pinning Shot, do I roll three times or get three Primary Dice?
faq.a: No. Roll once with 3 times the amount of dice you’d normally roll (e.g., Longbow 1d8 » 3d8).

faq.q: Nemesis makes everything my Quarry. Does every melee hit now give a charge?
faq.a: Yes.

classes.name: Mage
classes.tagline: Brilliant spellcasters with a wide arsenal of spells at their disposal.
classes.flavor:
Comprehending the Tapestry of Mana is no trivial endeavor—it will yield its arcane secrets only to the earnest seeker of knowledge. A mage refines their natural gifts through scholarly pursuit, with tomes and parchments as their companions, alongside the sage counsel of a seasoned mentor or three!

Yet, once the adept learns to discern the subtleties of its intricate patterns as it unfurls and meanders into the ethereal expanse—it is in that moment the apprentice truly ascends to the mantle of mage. This is the chosen path of those who would wield authority over the elements. Elemental power flows through all things… find it, study it, and harness it!
highlights: Customize your spells: stretch time, gain extra-dimensional vision, or echo cast multiple spells!
Rain fire from the heavens, freeze enemies in their tracks, and strike with thunderous bolts of lightning.
Demand Control or lean into the Chaos! What awaits you? Diamond Skin? Elemental Entanglement? Liquefied Legs?!

classes.flavor:
I will protect my companions and vanquish evil at all costs. Various orders of these zealous, holy warriors have attained great physical and radiant strength through absolute devotion to a higher power in the form of oaths.

Through their strength, both physical and radiant, nothing can sway them from their hunger for justice and their fervent pursuit and hatred of evil. The mark of a true Oathsworn, however, is their willingness to lay down their life for their friends.

Smite with righteous judgment. The more you face evil, the more potent your strikes become.

Stand as a bastion of defense, safeguarding allies even from afar. Bringing justice to every corner of the realm.

Mend wounds, and inspire others to embrace your noble cause with unwavering conviction.

faq.q: Are Judgment Dice used up on a miss?
faq.a: Yes, they are expended on your next attack, hit or miss (they also expire at the end of combat if unused).

faq.q: Can I used Judgment Dice on spells?
faq.a: On Reach spells, yes.

faq.q: Do I gain Judgment Dice when I Interpose?
faq.a: Yes, Interposing makes you the new target of the attack. You gain Judgment Dice even if a monster’s attack misses or all the damage is mitigated.

faq.q: Can Judgment Dice crit or explode?
faq.a: No. They are additional damage on an attack you make (but the underlying attack can crit as normal).

faq.q: Can I Interpose more than once if it’s free?
faq.a: No. Each reaction is still limited to 1/round even if free.

classes.name: Shadowmancer
classes.tagline: A shadowy master of expendable hordes. Flexible minion-based class with powerful spellcasting options.
classes.flavor:
Great power sometimes comes from… horrible places. But what’s the alternative, spend our entire lives… STUDYING?! Now that’s horrible. Who’d want to waste their lives reading books—learning magic the hard way? Work SMART, not hard. Just scheme up a way to take what you need from someone who won’t miss it—Ancient Horrors don’t guard their power nearly as well as you’d think! And if there’s power just lying around, it’d be dumb of me to not use it, really.

So what if I wear black and have to occasionally sacrifice an animal here and there while chanting? Does that automatically mean I’m evil? *Pfft,* hardly! Not every ANCIENT HORROR is the same; that’s like saying crow black and spider black are the same. Okay, bad examples, but the point stands. If you’re tired of swinging swords around and getting sweaty like a peasant, just summon a horde of Shadow minions to do your bidding. They’re always eager to serve!

Use your cunning to forge pacts with ancient, unfathomable entities, and draw upon their incomprehensible power.

Bend living Shadows to your will, summon them to swarm your foes, serving as both sword and fodder.

Empower your shadowy abilities with lesser and greater invocations from your master.

features.text: You and your allies can attack between spaces your Shadows occupy as if they were the same space. Gain advantage when attacking this way (e.g., an ally next to a Shadow can make a melee attack against any enemy also adjacent to a Shadow).

features.name: The Vast Cold
features.text: Your Shadows inflict the Slowed condition when attacked in melee.

features.name: Void Singularity
features.text: (Reach 1/Shadow) Whenever 1 or more Shadows move into the space of another Shadow, all of them implode and die, dealing their combined damage to all creatures in the area, moving them toward the center as you choose.

features.name: The Consuming Dark
features.text: (1/encounter) When a Shadow kills an enemy you may have it transform into a Greater Shadow.

features.name: Urgent Command
features.text: Gain a Wound to move your Shadows as a Reaction.

subclasses.name: Pact of the Endless Swarm
subclasses.flavor: Pests and vermin… Even the weakest grow strong in numbers. The denizens of your swarm are infinite and unyielding.

features.name: Summon Hive
features.text: Whenever you cast Summon Shadow, also summon a Hive within Reach 2 (max of INT Hives). **Hive.** Immobile minion, enemies within Reach 2 attack with disadvantage. At the end of your turns, spawns a swarm: roll and set aside 1d4. Whenever you or an ally attacks, you can expend any of these dice to increase the damage done.

features.name: Rampant Brood
features.text: When a Hive dies, it spawns 2 swarms. Whenever you cast Command Shadows, your Hives can also move.

features.name: Broodlord
features.text: You may spend your Interpose reaction to make a Hive Interpose for yourself or an ally instead.

features.name: Impending Infestation
features.text: Summon 1 additional Hive for each time you’ve previously cast Summon Shadow this encounter.

features.name: Terrible Plague
features.text: Your swarms increase to d8 damage and your Hives’ Reach increases to 3.

subclasses.name: Pact of the High Celestial
subclasses.flavor: Be not afraid! Your radiant spirits empower, bless, and protect those that you deem worthy.

features.name: Divine Bestowal
features.text: Your Shadows become radiant Spirits, lose their ability to attack directly, but can move into the space of an ally and bless them. They move wherever the ally does, and each one grants the ally +2 damage on their attacks and +2 damage reduction from incoming attacks. If an ally takes damage, all minions blessing them die.

features.name: Radiant Boon
features.text: You may target allies with Shadow Blast and give them temp HP instead of damaging them.

features.name: Divine Bestowal (2)
features.text: Your minions’ blessing increases to 3.

features.name: Celestial Armor
features.text: When a blessed ally Defends or Interposes, 1 minion blessing them can sacrifice itself to take the damage instead.

features.name: Apotheosis
features.text: (1/Safe Rest) For 1 round you are immune to all damage and negative effects. Anytime you would roll a d20, roll a d100 instead, and anytime you would roll less than a d20, roll a d20.

subclasses.name: Reaver
subclasses.flavor: Cast aside, born anew.
subclasses.intro: Hollow One. Cut off from your Patron, you can no longer cast Shadow Blast, nor can you cast tiered spells using Pilfered Power. However, as a parting token, you have stolen a secret from your Patron: the magical Bonescythe, a weapon of sinew and bone, infused with shadowy magic.

features.name: Shadow Exploit
features.text: Whenever you Defend, you can sacrifice a Shadow to take no damage. Or you may sacrifice a Shadow to cast a spell at the highest tier you have unlocked. Each subsequent time you use this ability in an encounter, increase the cost by 1 Shadow.

features.name: Grim Harrow
features.text: When you strike with your Bonescythe, treat each die as Primary. You may divide the dice as you choose amongst any number of adjacent targets within Reach.

features.name: Reap
features.text: When your Bonescythe crits or kills a creature, summon a Shadow for free (ignoring your Shadow Limit).

features.name: My Blood, My Power
features.text: You may take 1 Wound to cast a tiered spell you know at the highest tier you have unlocked.

features.name: Otherworldly Might
features.text: Advantage on Concentration saves if you have any Shadows.

features.name: Sovereign One
features.text: Summon 2 Shadows and your Bonescythe for free when you roll Initiative.

options.name: Summon Bonescythe
options.text: Summon a magical Bonescythe, a melee weapon. (Reach 2) 2d12 slashing+DEX necrotic damage to EACH die (add 1 extra damage die every 5 Levels). On hit (or when combat ends): it shatters and must be resummoned to use again. Invocations affecting Shadow Blast affect your Bonescythe instead.

faq.q: Does Hungering Shadows or Swarming Shadows combo with Shadow Rush?
faq.a: No. Hungering Shadows and Swarming Shadows require you to roll the max amount; Shadow Rush forgoes rolling dice.

faq.q: Can I go over my Shadow Limit?
faq.a: Some spells and abilities may permit this, but while at or above your Shadow Limit, casting Summon Shadow has no effect.

faq.q: How do minions and swarms interact with Armor?
faq.a: Add up all the minions’/swarms’ dice and treat them as a single attack.

classes.name: Shepherd
classes.tagline: A flexible pet-based support class that can dole out healing and harm with equal mastery.
classes.flavor:
Thou shalt revere the gifts of life and death, neither of which is ever given or taken. Rather, we are all merely journeying from this realm and that of the beyond. But alas, often do these wandering souls find themselves bereft of guidance.

Thus falls upon the Shepherd the solemn duty—to be a beacon of light to those ensnared in darkness, and darkness to those who, in hubris, deem themselves to be the light. For many, the journey of service is a difficult path—yet, in this task we are not solitary. Our Lifebinding Spirits, the steadfast companions of our faith, are bound beside us, comforting and aiding us in the stewardship we’ve been given.

Summon a faithful companion to your side to provide invaluable support in battle.

Embrace the balance of life and death, bolster allies with healing spells and boons.

Smite foes with radiant fury or wither enemies with dark necrotic power.

sidebars.text: After spending a day tending to a sacred place or serving others during a Safe Rest, you may choose different Shepherd options available to you.

sidebars.text: Your Lifebinding Spirit can take the form of any Small/Tiny friendly creature (dog, lamb, rabbit, sparrow, etc.). Give your little buddy a name, too! Outside of combat, your companion is a spirit, so it can pass through walls and dangers harmlessly and briefly move away from you (but always prefers to be faithfully at your side). It cannot speak.

sidebars.title: Rushed Attacks and My Companion?

options.name: Vengeful Spirit
options.text: (AoE Reach 2) Your Lifebinding Spirit sacrifices itself to deal its Harm damage to all enemies within Reach.

subclasses.flavor: With death as your companion, you can unleash dark powers on your foes.

features.name: Soul Reaper

features.name: Harbinger of Decay
features.text: Vibrant colors and lovely smells are suppressed near you. Foods spoil more rapidly in your presence, and you frequently awaken to flies wherever you lodge. You may have your Lifebinding Spirit shift into a deathly version of itself (a zombie dog, a devious imp, etc.) and have its damage type become necrotic.

features.text: (1/Safe Rest) Reaction (when you would drop to 0 HP): Drop to 1 HP instead and your Lifebinding Spirit crits the attacker back.

features.name: Deathbringer’s Touch

features.name: Conduit of Death
features.text: Your Veilwalker’s Blessing ability recharges when you roll Initiative.

subclasses.name: Luminary of Mercy
subclasses.flavor: Save the dying, wield the light, embody your virtue. Your compassion makes you a worthy vessel for radiant energy.

features.name: Merciful Healing
features.text: You can use Mend on non-Dying creatures. While you are Dying, your Lifebinding Spirit can act 1/round without spending an action.

features.name: Life is Beautiful
features.text: Harmless and lovely creatures such as butterflies and hummingbirds are attracted to your presence and often follow you. Flowers bloom more vibrantly in your presence.

features.name: Searing Light
features.text: 1 Action: (Reach 6) Whenever you heal HP, you may expend 1 use of Mend to damage another target for the amount of HP recovered.

features.name: Powerful Healer
features.text: (WIL/Safe Rest) Whenever you would heal HP, you may instead give that many temp HP, OR heal the max amount you could roll.

features.name: Lifebinder’s Embrace
features.text: Your Mend may heal 1 additional creature. Regain 1 charge of Mend when you roll Initiative (this expires if unspent at the end of combat).

subclasses.name: Luminary of Protection
subclasses.flavor: “An ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure. Why wait for your friends to get hurt to heal them when you could prevent them from being hurt in the first place?”

features.name: Guardian Spirit
features.text: Whenever you Interpose, you may have your Lifebinding Spirit do so instead by spending one of its Mend charges.

features.name: Ready for Danger
features.text: +WIL Initiative, you may give this bonus to 1 ally as well (after they roll).

features.name: Shield of Light
features.text: You may have your healing spells grant temp HP instead. (1/encounter) You can use Mend without spending a charge.

features.name: Ever Vigilant
features.text: Gain advantage on Initiative. You and 1 ally gain +1 action at the start of each encounter.

subclasses.name: Luminary of the Forge
subclasses.flavor: “Your Lifebinding Spirit is the furnace’s flame incarnate.”

features.name: Flameworker
features.text: Exchange knowledge of the Necrotic spell school for Fire. Your Lifebinding Spirit inflicts Smoldering on crit.

features.name: Seasoned Journeyman
features.text:
Whenever you Safe Rest, choose one:
• **Weaponsmith.** Your weapons gain +STR damage until your next Safe Rest.
• **Armorsmith.** Your armor gains +STR Defense until your next Safe Rest.

features.name: Lightforged
features.text: Mend also grants WIL+STR temp HP and 1 action.

features.name: Living Ember
features.text: Your Lifebinding Spirit deals 2× damage to Smoldering targets, ending the condition.

features.name: Masterwork
features.text: +WIL to Weaponsmith and Armorsmith; you may choose twice.

features.name: Quench the Blaze
features.text: (1/encounter) When a Smoldering enemy loses the condition, you may Restrain them until the end of their next turn.

faq.q: Does my companion have its own HP and actions?
faq.a: No. It has no HP of its own HP and acts only when directed by you.

faq.q: Do I have to summon my companion every encounter?
faq.a: No. Once summoned, it remains faithfully by your side untill dismissed.

faq.q: Can enemies attack my companion? Does it take up space?
faq.a: No.

faq.q: Rushed Attacks and My Companion?
faq.a: You and your companion use the same action pool, but count as different creatures. So you can each attack once without Rushed Attacks every round. Teamwork!

faq.q: Can my hero miss on purpose to trigger Deathbringer’s Touch?
faq.a: No. A hero does not try to miss on purpose.

classes.name: Songweaver
classes.tagline: A high utility class that can harm, harass, and heal with equal mastery!
classes.flavor:
Each Songweaver holds a spark granted to them by a muse at birth; a spark which fuels their creative energy and flows forth in the form of a sharp wit, relentless humor, or moving art.

The power of a Songweaver’s spark is also evident in their powerful sway over others. Songweavers can bolster and infuse courage in their allies, or… make their enemies’ brains leak out through their ears. The Songweaver can bring a whole new meaning to verbal abuse! They can even redirect the (often justified) attacks of others, in order to protect their own moneymakers. As a Songweaver, you can:

Charm the hapless people you meet and inspire your allies to reach fantastic new heights of heroism!

Use your Lyrical Weaponry and powerful charisma to dominate enemies—even redirecting attacks, making enemies attack their own allies!

Control the Battlefield with a chord of chaos, a rad heroic ballad, or a debilitating rhapsody.

sidebars.text: Whenever you perform in a place that inspires you, or exchange barbs with another competent wordsmith during a Safe Rest, you may choose different Songweaver options available to you.

sidebars.title: Flavor is Free
sidebars.text: If you’d rather have a more traditional bard type—a keeper of ancient legends—instead of people you know, the characters above can be reflavored as famous legends from history that you can magically summon via song. Feel free to work with your GM to make it happen. As long as the mechanics stay roughly the same, have fun!

sidebars.title: Making Your Own People
sidebars.text: You can work with your GM to swap out Stompy, Gran Gran, Mal, and Linos for your own creations if you like. 1 in-combat person whose damage scales with your Level (see other spells and abilities for appropriate amounts of damage or other effects), 1 out-of-combat support person, 1 who can help in narrative situations, and 1 who can give sporadic utility. Follow that broad pattern and you’ll be fine!

sidebars.title: Balance Note
sidebars.text: If you find yourself never wanting to use one, make it slightly stronger; if you’re using it too frequently, consider bringing the power Level down slightly or adding some other drawback.

optionGroups.intro: Perform! Whenever you perform in a place that inspires you, or exchange barbs with another competent wordsmith during a Safe Rest, you may choose different Songweaver options available to you.

options.name: Heroic Ballad
options.text: +2 max Songweaver’s Inspiration charges. When used to reroll an ally’s attack, your Songweaver’s Inspiration also grants them +WIL damage.

options.name: Inspiring Anthem
options.text: (1/encounter) Grant all friendly Dying creatures who can hear you 1 HP and 1 action.

options.name: Not My Beautiful Faaace!
options.text: (1/encounter) When you Defend, force the attacker to choose another target within range on a failed WIL save (if there is none, the attack fails). If they fail by 5 or more, they attack themselves! On save, reroll the attack and choose either result.

options.name: Rhapsody of the Normal
options.text: When you roll 4+ on Vicious Mockery, you may spend a Songweaver’s Inspiration charge to temporarily suppress any special abilities they have until the end of their next turn. They can do only what an untrained average villager can do, attack once for 1d4 damage and move up to 6 spaces (no Armor, spellcasting, flying, regeneration, other inherent or trained features).

options.name: Song of Domination
options.text: (Reach 6, 1/encounter) Move all enemies who can hear you 6 spaces on a failed WIL save, half as far on save. They cannot move on their next turn.

options.name: Stompy
options.text: Summon a huge hill giant for 1 round. As he enters the battlefield adjacent to you, use Stompy’s Stomp: Make a DC 10 Influence check. On a success, he moves 6 spaces in a direction you choose; on a failure, he moves toward YOU instead (“YOU NOT FRIEND!”). He deals LVL+Influence check damage to everything in his path. ANY other creature within Reach 6 of Stompy can use this ability once instead of an attack.

options.name: Mal, the Malevolent Imp
options.text: Summon a tiny fiend for 1 night. He can find out dangerous information you have no right to know! Or “take care” of a problem with only the slightest chance of things going wrong. Make an Influence check to convince him to help you (advantage if you ask him to do something he would find mischievous or fun; with disadvantage if it is something he would find good or menial).

options.name: Gran Gran (NOT a hag)
options.text: When resting, you may summon her for 1 hour to soothe your wounds (and hassle you for not eating enough). She bakes and hands out WIL+INT pastries. Eating one recovers one mana, Hit Die, or Wound. Eat them while they’re warm! They expire in 10 minutes.

options.name: Linos, the Everfriendly
options.text: Summon a legendary flying (but friendly) creature to take you and your party wherever you need to go. He may request a very large amount of food as payment.

subclasses.name: Herald of Snark
subclasses.flavor: Nothing wrong with a little lighthearted jest now and again! Distract and discourage your enemies with tricks of the mind.

features.name: Opportunistic Snark
features.text: Reaction (Range 12, when an enemy misses an attack): You may cast Vicious Mockery at them; it deals double damage when cast this way and can’t miss.

features.name: Fight Picker

features.name: Chord of Chaos

features.name: Words Like Swords
features.text: Your Vicious Mockery damage die becomes 1d12.

subclasses.name: Herald of Courage
subclasses.flavor: “Brave heroes! Lend your ears to my epic tale…” Be heartened, and your friends will never falter.

features.name: Inspiring Presence
features.text: Whichever ally is nearest to you has advantage (if multiple are equally close, choose your favorite).

features.name: Fire in My Bones
features.text: Your Songweaver’s Inspiration also grants your target 1 additional action.

features.name: Unfailing Resolve
features.text: Your Songweaver’s Inspiration allows your target to reroll with advantage or increases a die face by +2.

features.name: Chorus of Champions
features.text: (1/encounter) Free Reaction: Give all party members 1 action.

subclasses.name: Herald of Singing Steel
subclasses.flavor: Your blade cuts as deeply as your wit. Choose this subclass if you want to blend musical mastery with deadly bladework.

features.name: Songwoven Blade
features.text: Whenever you make a melee attack, you can apply the damage and all other effects of your Vicious Mockery to it.

features.name: Ha-HA!
features.text: Creatures Taunted by you are also Weakened 10 on their first attack each round.

features.name: From the Chandelier!
features.text: (1/encounter) Vault off a nearby obstacle and move for free (ignoring enemy spaces and Difficult Terrain); gaining advantage on your next attack.

features.name: Riposte
features.text: Reaction (when a creature attacks you in melee but deals you no damage): You may attack them with Songwoven Blade, rolling a d20 as your Primary Die instead.

features.name: Ballad Blade
features.text: Creatures Taunted by you are Weakened 20 on their first attack each round instead.

subclasses.name: Herald of Torment
subclasses.flavor: Songweavers are often thought of as musicians that play uplifting songs and tell hopeful stories, but a Herald of Torment uses that same ability to poison the minds of their foes.

features.name: Poison Mind
features.text: Instead of Taunting, your Vicious Mockery Poisons the target’s mind (until you Poison another creature this way).

features.name: Tormented Mind

features.name: Legendkeeper

features.name: Legend’s Tale

Cantrip, 1 Action (Reach 8). Summon a hero of legend to aid you for the duration of this encounter (max 1). Each Legend can also be Exerted as a Reaction to provide an additional powerful effect—but afterward it leaves the battlefield. **Legends you know:**
**The Aegis.** Friendly creatures in a 3×3 area gain +WIL damage reduction. Exert: Whenever an ally in the area Interposes they may take no damage instead.
**The Stiletto.** Friendly creatures in a 3×3 area can move or hide for free (1/turn). Exert (Reach 12): Whenever an ally would crit, add INT d12 damage to the attack.

features.name: You may have up to 2 Legends active at a time
features.text:
You also learn the following Legends:
**The Mender.** Friendly creatures in a 3×3 area can end 1 negative condition on themselves at the end of their turns. Exert: When a creature in the area drops to 0 HP you may revive them to LVL HP, they regain 1 action.
**The Tactician.** Friendly creatures in a 3×3 area have +2 to Reach, Range, and Assess rolls. Exert: (Reach 12) When an ally Assesses, they succeed and can choose twice.

features.name: Banner Bearer
features.text:
Whenever you would move you may move a summoned Legend instead. Learn the following Legends:
**The Warlord.** ALL creatures in a 3×3 area are Empowered 10. Exert: (Reach 12) ALL creatures are Empowered 10 until the end of their next turn.
**Old Oakum.** Creatures in a 3×3 area are Slowed and cannot fly. Exert: When a creature would exit the area pull them back into it and Restrain them.

features.name: Living Legends
features.text: Summon a Legend whenever you roll Initiative. (1/encounter) Whenever a Legend would depart the battlefield, you may instead allow it to stay and it does not count against your normal maximum.

faq.q: Can I Inspire myself?
faq.a: No. You are your own biggest fan, but you are not your own ally.

faq.q: When do I decide to use Songweaver’s Inspiration?
faq.a: After a roll, before the effect takes place.

faq.q: Does a rerolled Primary Die remain the Primary Die?
faq.a: Yes.

faq.q: Can increasing a die by 1 change a miss into a hit, or a hit into a crit?
faq.a: Yes.

faq.q: How do Legends work?
faq.a: They are incorporeal beings, immune to harm, and take up no space.

classes.name: Stormshifter
classes.tagline: A high utility class that can both harm and heal with equal mastery!
classes.flavor:
The trees whisper their excitement, the clouds sing with glee. Rejoice! The Master of Storm & Fang arrives. Legend speaks of an ancient union between mortal and dryad—beings capable of wielding lightning and tempests as others wield blade and shield. This is but half the tale.

Wanderers recount encounters with beings, some wise and benevolent, others fearsome, with claws that sparked with lightning and pelts sharp as daggers. They are as one with storm and beast, embodying the serene beauty and raw power of nature’s grace.
highlights: Aid your allies in whatever role is most needed. Damage, healing, or control.
Wade into the fray as a shapeshifted beast ranging from friendly to vicious, indomitable, or HORRIBLE.
Cast powerful spells from a distance to strike down, control, mend, and more.

options.name: Fearsome Beast
options.text:
Transform into a Large beast. Gain WIL Defense, WIL+LVL temp HP, advantage on STR saves, and:
Fearsome. Whenever you Interpose or Defend, you may spend 1 mana to force the attacker to reroll the attack (you must choose either result).
Gore. 1 Action: 1d8+LVL damage, on hit: gain LVL temp HP.

options.text:
Transform into a Medium beast. Gain +DEX Speed, you can move DEX spaces for free each turn, advantage on DEX saves, and:

Sting. 1 Action: (1/round, Reach 0) 1d4+3×LVL acid damage (ignoring Armor), on crit: Dazed.

options.name: Keen Senses

faq.q: Does shifting into a harmless beast have a time limit or take a charge?
faq.a: No.

faq.q: Can I cast spells while shifted?
faq.a: Yes. But it ends the form (unless you have a special ability that allows you to maintain it).

faq.q: When shifting between one Direbeast Form and another, do I keep the temp HP and Frenzy bonuses?
faq.a: Yes, though they end when combat does if unspent. The other passive effects (e.g., extra Defense or movement) are not maintained.

faq.q: Can I build up advantage with Frenzy then cast a spell with it?
faq.a: Yes. Have fun!

faq.q: Does the temp HP from Fearsome Beast and Gore stack?
faq.a: No. Temp HP do not stack.

faq.q: Can I Beastshift while Dying?
faq.a: Yes. Although dropping to 0 HP ends any currently active forms, you can shift again while Dying.

classes.name: The Cheat
classes.tagline: High burst damage class that can get in and get out!
classes.flavor:
The Cheat doesn’t call herself a Cheat, of course—rather, a streetsmart rogue, a survivalist, or a liberator of unused goods. They are masters of stealth, pickpocketing, and smooth talking. Some of the more vicious ilk are masters of death-dealing as well.

Cheats can be found in every city and byway under countless different names, but they all believe something similar: It’s a cruel, merciless world, and those who aim to survive don’t have time for silly things like “morals” or “honor.” Those are luxuries of the rich and powerful. Honor gets you killed—survival is about taking what you want, when you can.
highlights: Break the rules! You can change the dice you roll to whatever numbers suit you best!
Sneakily backstab enemies with devastating crits. Take down even heavily armored foes with a single blow!
Fight dirty with pocket sand and low blows. When things turn ugly, disappear and live to cheat another day!

You’re a well-rounded cheater. Gain the following abilities:
• (1/round) You may either Move or Hide for free.
• (1/Safe Rest) You may change any of your skill checks to 10+INT.
• If you roll less than 10 on Initiative, you may change it to 10 instead.
• You may gain advantage on skill checks while playing any games, competitions, or placing wagers. If you’re caught though…

features.text: +1 to any 2 of your stats. When you attack with a blade, you do not require targets to be Distracted to trigger Vicious Opportunist.

sidebars.title: Distracted
sidebars.text: A target is Distracted if it is adjacent to (or Taunted by) an ally, or if it cannot see you. Yes! If you can figure out how to attack on someone else’s turn, you can use this again in the same round!

sidebars.title: Magic?
sidebars.text: The Cheat has some abilities that look magical—they might be, but don’t have to be. You have your ways, okay? No need to explain how you did that, not even to the GM!

sidebars.title: Trade Secrets
sidebars.text: Whenever you spend a night talking shop with other roguish types during a Safe Rest, you may choose different Cheat options available to you.

options.name: “Creative” Accounting
options.text: Steal up to INT actions from your next turn (Gain up to INT actions now. The next time you would gain actions, subtract the number stolen). You cannot use this 2 turns in a row.

options.name: Exploit Weakness
options.text: Whenever you successfully Assess: Create an Opening against a creature, you can use Vicious Opportunist against them, even if they are not Distracted. This lasts for 1 minute or until you use it against another target.

options.name: Feinting Attack
options.text: If you miss for the 2nd time in a single round, you may change the Primary Die roll to any result instead.

options.name: How’d YOU get here?!
options.text: (Reach 12) “Teleport” adjacent to a Distracted target, and make a melee attack against them. If you crit, you may “teleport” again.

options.name: I’m Outta Here!
options.text: When an ally within Reach 4 is crit, you may turn Invisible until the end of your next turn and then move up to half your Speed for free.

options.name: Misdirection
options.text: Gain INT Defense. Whenever you Defend, you may halve the damage instead.

options.name: Steal Tempo
options.text: When you crit for the second time in a round, your target is Dazed and you give an ally 1 action.

options.name: Sunder Armor
options.text: After you crit an armored creature, sunder their armor: give the next non-crit Primary Die rolled against them +2.

options.name: Tangling Wire
options.text: Whenever you Grapple, you may Restrain instead.

options.name: The Setup
options.text: Reaction (when an ally misses a creature adjacent to you): You can make an Opportunity Attack against them, treating them as Distracted.

options.name: Trickshot
options.text: You can use Vicious Opportunist on thrown weapon attacks (but you can’t use Twist the Blade on them). Whenever you throw a weapon, you may spend an additional action to have it hit another creature within Reach 2 of it, dealing half as much damage to them.

subclasses.name: Tools of the Silent Blade
subclasses.flavor: Kill, kill, kill.

features.name: Amidst All This Commotion…
features.text: If a creature dies while you Sneak Attack them, you may turn Invisible until you attack again or until the beginning of your next turn.

features.name: Leave No Trace
features.text: Advantage on Stealth checks when you are at full health.

features.name: Cunning Strike
features.text: Deal +2×INT damage whenever you crit.

features.name: Professional Skulker
features.text: Gain a climbing Speed and advantage on Stealth checks (replaces Leave No Trace).

features.name: KILL
features.text: When you Sneak Attack an enemy with fewer max HP than you, it dies.

subclasses.name: Tools of the Scoundrel
subclasses.flavor: Stay alive, fight dirty.

features.name: Low Blow
features.text:
When you Sneak Attack a creature not already Taunted by you, you may spend 1 additional action to roll 1d4. They are:
1. Taunted by you for the rest of this encounter.
2. Knocked Prone, then Taunted by you for the rest of this encounter.
3. Dazed, then Taunted by you for the rest of this encounter.
4. Incapacitated until the end of the next hero’s turn.

features.name: Sweet Talk
features.text: You may gain advantage on all Influence checks with NPCs you’ve just met for the first time. This lasts until you fail an Influence check with them or until you meet a 2nd time. You have disadvantage on Influence checks with them after you use this ability (until you get back on their good side).

features.name: Pocket Sand
features.text: (2/encounter—you’ve got to collect more sand!) When you Defend against an adjacent creature, Blind the attacker until the start of their next turn and force them to reroll the attack (Blind creatures attack with disadvantage).

features.name: Escape Plan
features.text: (1/Safe Rest) When you would drop to 0 HP or gain a Wound, you don’t. Instead, you turn Invisible for 1 minute or until you attack.

features.name: Heads I Win, Tails You Lose
features.text: (1/encounter) Attacks you make this round don’t miss, you crit on 1 less than normally needed, and you gain LVL temp HP.

subclasses.name: Tools of the Serpent
subclasses.flavor: You have harnessed the terrible fangs of nature to her deadly array of poisons. Choose this subclass if you want to debilitate your foes with venom and viciousness.

features.name: Viper’s Kiss
features.text: Creatures you damage become Poisoned until the end of their next turn. Creatures Poisoned this way are also Distracted.

features.name: I’ve Tried This One Before
features.text: You have advantage on saves against poison. Additionally, you can identify any poison you inspect.

features.name: Noxious Cloud
features.text: (1/encounter, Reach 4) Action: Enemies in a 2×2 area take INT d6 damage (ignoring armor) and become Poisoned. Creatures already Poisoned are also Dazed.

features.name: Cruel Dose
features.text: Creatures Poisoned by you are also Slowed and their attack Range is halved.

features.name: Volatile Toxins
features.text: Noxious Cloud can be used twice each encounter. Whenever a creature Poisoned by you dies, their body erupts into a Noxious Cloud.

subclasses.name: Tools of the Gambler
subclasses.flavor: Trust me—this time it’s a SURE THING. Choose this subclass if you want to risk it all with dangerous plays and walk the line of ruin.

features.name: All In
features.text: When you Sneak Attack, you may go All In: Roll a single All In die; if it rolls higher than average, maximize ALL of your Sneak Attack dice; otherwise minimize them.

features.name: That Was Just a Practice Roll
features.text: (1/encounter) You may reroll ANY die.

features.name: It’s All Fun and Games
features.text: If you’re caught cheating at a game, competition, or wager, you gain advantage on skill checks to get out of the consequences.

features.name: Pocket Aces!
features.text: (1/Safe Rest) You can set a friendly creature’s Initiative roll to 20.

features.name: Double or Nothing!

classes.tagline: A furiously fast melee class that can deliver and avoid terrible blows.
classes.flavor:
A Zephyr dedicates their life to the relentless pursuit of kinetic prowess. They hone their bodies into blurs of motion, training from a young age in remote wilds or mountain monasteries, wielding speed to unleash blows that echo through their foes and slip past attacks like a whispering wind. Speed is both their weapon and shield.

Through ceaseless training, they harness their inner momentum to achieve feats of supernatural agility, executing every motion with flowing precision.
highlights: You’re a relentless force on the battlefield. Absorb blows and deliver devastating strikes.
Move with unparalleled speed and determination, outpacing your allies and foes alike.
Retaliate with precision and turn enemy strikes into opportunities for devastating counterattacks.

faq.q: What does Slipstream’s move 1 space do?

classes.name: Manawright
classes.tagline: An inventive, toolbox class equally capable wherever needed.
classes.flavor:
They call me when the airship stalls mid-descent, when the arcane relay spirals out of phase, or when the golem starts speaking in languages it wasn’t programmed to know. Don’t mind the dents—took a few kicks to get her started, is all. Still works lovely. Just… don’t stand too close when she hums like that, and if she starts whistling in B flat—RUN!”

Your workshop might be a cluttered shrine to chaos or an immaculate studio thrumming with pristine energy—whatever the setting, the Manawright gets to work. Some call you a mad tinkerer—a hazard to public safety. Others speak in hushed awe of your sleek designs, machines tuned with impossible precision. Your genius is fueled by raw instinct and sharpened calculation. You don’t build for show. You don’t build for fame. You build because it’s who you are—and the world needs what you can make.

sidebars.title: At a Glance
sidebars.text:
Wield inventions that defy reality—from mana-forged blades, to gravity-snaring tethercoils, and boots that laugh at gravity.

The more you push your inventions, the more they deliver—but push too far and your gear might malfunction!

Retool gadgets mid-battle or improvise fixes under fire; you can adapt your arsenal as needed.

sidebars.title: Powering Inventions
sidebars.text:
When using an invention, you may expend any amount of available Mana Dice. The more you utilize at a time, the greater the effect—but the greater the risk. If any Mana Die rolls a number less than or equal to the total number of them, the invention overloads, triggering a Mishap.

Example. If you spend 3 Mana Dice at a time, if any of them rolls 3 or less you get a Mishap!

sidebars.title: Reconfigure!
sidebars.text: You may choose different Manawright options whenever you tinker at your workshop during a Safe Rest.

sidebars.title: Damage type?
sidebars.text: Whenever you create or upgrade an invention you can choose a reasonable damage type. Lightning, Fire, or Piercing damage for the Manabolt Cannon? Makes sense! Necrotic or Ice? Maybe, check with your GM!

sidebars.title: Make it your own!
sidebars.text: If you’d rather have a chainsaw sword rather than a mana blade, go for it! The Mana Dice can be “Rev Dice” as you rev up the engine before slicing. Or if you prefer more of a steampunk aesthetic, or magitech, or anything else—feel free to flavor the inventions in a way that suits you best.

+4 Range/Mana Die (min 1). Choose 1 mode:

**Charge: Coil.** 2 Actions: (1/encounter) Creatures fully in an area equal to the number of Mana Dice Rolled (e.g., 2 dice: 2×2 area) are Restrained until the end of their next turn.

**Upgrades:**

features.name: Potion-sense

features.name: Refined Formulas

options.name: Alchemist’s Fire

(3×3 AoE) Sum the Mana Dice and add 5 to each, deal that much damage to creatures in the area.
**Mishap: Overcombustion.** 1×1 or 5×5 area (GM’s choice).

options.name: Propulsion Potion

options.name: Liquid Lightning
options.text: (0 Actions to consume) Drink at any time, even on another creature’s turn (e.g., to Defend): gain extra Mana Dice equal to your max. They’re lost when your Mana Accumulator recharges, and they can trigger mishaps as normal.

options.name: Bottled Luck
options.text: (3×3 AoE, +1 area per MD spent) Creatures in the area gain your choice of advantage or disadvantage on rolls this round for each Mana Die spent. **Mishap: Bad luck.** 1×1 or 5×5 area (GM’s choice).

options.name: Petrification Potion
options.text: Give a creature 20 temp HP/Mana Die, they are Incapacitated for as long as these HP last (friendly creatures can end this early). 30 temp HP are lost at the beginning of that creature’s turn. **Mishap: Petrified Mana Channels.** –1 max Mana Die until cleared (DC: 10 Might check).

options.name: Aberrant Brew
options.text: Grow or shrink a creature 1 size larger or smaller for 1 round (until the start of your next turn). **Bigger:** Empowered 5 per Mana Die; their attacks and attacks against them have advantage. **Smaller:** Weakened 5 per Mana Die; their attacks and attacks against them have disadvantage. **Mishap: Unexpected Side Effects.** A 2nd nearby creature gains the same effect (GM’s choice).

features.name: Chronal Tinkerer
features.text: Invent the Chronal Device.

features.name: Temporal Reach
features.text: +2 Reach on Timetinker.

features.name: Timethief
features.text: (1/encounter) Action: A creature within Reach skips their next turn (effects that end at the end of their next turn don’t end yet).

features.name: Master of Time

features.name: Master of Moments

options.name: Chronal Device
options.text:
Timetinker. 0 Actions. (Reach 4, 1/turn) Spend a Mana Die to:
• **Movement:** A creature can move twice or half as far (including Interpose) for each Mana Die spent.
• **Assess:** Roll with advantage or choose another option for each Mana Die spent.
• **Attacks:** Add (or subtract) 1 from the Primary Die for each Mana Die spent.
• **Mishap:** Timefracture. GM chooses an enemy to immediately take an action.

faq.q: Mishaps
faq.a: Only Mana Dice rolled in an initial attack are taken into account for Mishaps. Any additional dice are ignored (e.g., additional dice from crits or advantage).

faq.q: Primary Die
faq.a: The d6 for the Thunder Gauntlets is always used as the Primary Die (while your Mana Dice are d6s, whichever d6 lands leftmost is the Primary Die), likewise for the Manabolt Cannon’s d12. For the Manablade since there is no base weapon die, whichever Mana Die lands leftmost is the Primary Die.

faq.q: How does Advantage/Disadvantage work with inventions?
faq.a: As normal, roll 1 additional Primary Die and the lowest/highest is removed.

faq.q: I’ve Got JUST the thing!
faq.a: “Simple” as in: an iron wedge, a wrench, a lockpick, block & tackle, tripwire, etc. NOT “an anti-gravity device.”

faq.q: Kinetic Redirect
faq.a: You can’t knock a target upward (unless you are below them somehow).

faq.q: Stable Admixtures
faq.a: This does not count toward your 2/encounter Battlebrew limit, nor does it take an action to brew since it’s ready by the time you enter combat.

classes.name: Hexbinder
classes.flavor:
They come to her with trembling pleas: a child’s fever, a lover’s betrayal, a shadow too heavy to lift. She listens, sharp-eyed, and offers what fits—balm or bane, as the need demands. But cross her, and you’ll learn: the tongue that soothes can whisper your doom, and the hands that mend can twist your fate to ruin.

A hexbinder’s magic is neither flashy nor kind. It’s practical, rooted in the muck and murmur of the old world—salves whispered over flame, curses knotted into thread, remedies older than the hills. She mends the broken and breaks the foolish, her hands stained with both mercy and malice.

“Plagued by a cough, my lovely? A festering wound? A stain on your spirit? Sip this down, you’ll feel right as rain by morning—don’t mind the taste, it’s meant to be bitter!”

optionGroups.name: Afflictions
optionGroups.intro: You can Afflict a max of 1 creature at a time with a max of INT different Afflictions. Afflictions last for as long as you maintain Concentration (DC 10 STR save when crit).

options.name: Brittle
options.text: Target suffers 1 damage for each space it moves (or is moved). Level 10: 2 damage/space.

options.name: Dimmed
options.text: Target has disadvantage 2 when attacking beyond Range/Reach 1.

options.name: Doomed
options.text: (1/encounter) Maximize the next roll against Afflicted target.

options.name: Enfeebled
options.text: Target falls Prone at the end of each of your turns.

options.name: Word of Decay

faq.q: Bloodcurse
faq.a: Its damage is calculated vs a single target, before any reductions from Defense or other sources. This spell is secret to the target, not the GM.

faq.q: Brittle
faq.a: Teleporting and swapping places don’t trigger it; moving, being moved, and falling do.

faq.q: Circle of Thorns
faq.a: An enemy already adjacent when it’s cast hasn’t entered; being pushed in counts.

faq.q: Coven
faq.a: Spells from your Coven school can be upcast (up to your highest tier) and Diminished.

faq.q: Doomed
faq.a: Maximizes only dice rolled against the target (e.g., not Fury or Judgment Dice). It can crit, but the extra crit die is rolled normally. In an AoE, only the Doomed creature takes max damage.

faq.q: Familiar
faq.a: It’s smart enough to take care of itself in combat—no need to track its HP, location, or commands; its boons cover what it does for you. Outside combat, you might bribe or cajole it into something moderately risky, but scouting a whole dungeon alone almost certainly won’t work (and won’t be fun for others!). You can’t take the same boon twice.

faq.q: Futuresight Dice
faq.a: They can change any die, including the tens die of a d44, d66, or d88.

faq.q: Mark of Protection
faq.a: A protected creature dropped to 0 HP can stay at 1 HP instead of Dying.

faq.q: Multiple Hexbinders
faq.a: Each counts only their own Afflictions, and the same Affliction from two Hexbinders doesn’t stack.

faq.q: Pact of Enmity
faq.a: No dice are rolled, so it never crits.

faq.q: Pestilential Reign
faq.a: If you already know Pestilent, choose a different Affliction.

faq.q: Wyrding Strands

classes.name: Psion
classes.tagline: High risk, high reward class that controls the battlefield through positioning and psionic power!
classes.flavor:
Each creature that lives and breathes is united by one shared experience: THOUGHT. Psions take this fundamental reality and harness it as a tool in the physical world. Bend the flow gravity, twist the reality of minds, or throw things really, really hard. All of this barely scratches the surface of what a Psion can accomplish: altering the physical world through sheer thought alone.

Psionic power, rare and mighty as it is, takes a toll on those who dare to wield it. To exert one's own mind so as to affect the world and other minds around you is to take on all the latent negative thoughts that can be found there. However, those with the will to withstand the strain can achieve heights that few could ever dream of.

Control your psionic field, taking command of errant objects, friends, and foes in your surroundings.

Withstand the strain! Push yourself to greater heights with your Psionic abilities at the cost of your fortitude.

Dominate minds. Take control over the thoughts and perceptions of your enemies through illusions and misdirections.

Gain a Strain Die (1d6). Roll them when your turn ends, if any rolls a 1, your Concentration breaks.

optionGroups.intro: Requires your Psionic Field to be active. All ongoing Psionic abilities end if your concentration is broken.

options.name: Psionic Strike
options.text: +1 damage for each Strain Die you have. When you attack you may gain 1 Strain to ignore all disadvantage and attack with advantage instead.

options.name: Kinetic Launch
options.text: Launch a willing ally within your Psionic Field up to 8 spaces. They can use a reaction to make an Opportunity Attack against a creature within their Reach as they move. Gain 1 Strain to grant them advantage on the attack instead of disadvantage

options.name: Psionic Blast

options.name: Dominate Mind

options.name: Atomize Weapon
options.text: Gain up to KEY Strain. Explode a weapon within your Psionic field then reform it perfectly as it was. Deal the sum of your Strain Dice to all others within your Psionic Field.

options.name: Psionic Lockdown
options.text: Enemies entering your Psionic field suffer LVL damage, Enemies within your Psionic field cannot leave. Projectiles have their damage reduced by LVL. 1 Strain/round to maintain.

options.name: Levitate
options.text: 1 willing medium or smaller creature, treat them as if they are anywhere within your field (e.g. for Interposing, attacking etc.) (they can move freely within your psionic field on their turn). +1 Strain/round.

options.name: Dampening Field
options.text: Creatures inside your Psionic Field take 10 less damage from ranged attacks originating outside it this round. +1 Strain.

options.name: Reactive Mind
options.text: Reaction: when you Defend, you may gain 1 Strain to push the attacker 4 spaces.

options.name: Mindrend
options.text: Explode a creature’s mind. +1-3 strain dice. The next time you roll your Strain Dice, deal that much damage to an enemy (ignoring armor).

options.name: Control Projectiles
options.text: Reaction, if your total number Strain Dice are greater than the Primary Die of a ranged attack, redirect the attack at another creature within Range. +Strain. Extra range/damage.

options.name: Sudden Shift
options.text: Reaction. When an ally within your Psionic Field Defends, push them 1 space, the attack misses. Gain 2 Strain.

subclasses.name: Adept of Bladestorm
subclasses.flavor: "Dual wielding, huh? Watch this!"

features.name: Bladebearer
features.text: Your weapons wielded with your Psionic Field are considered dual wielded. When you gain Strain while using Psionic Strike, add the Strain Die as damage.

features.name: Bladestorm
features.text: (1/encounter) Others within your Psionic Field take KEY damage for each space they move (or are moved) this round. +2 Strain.

features.name: Shieldstorm
features.text: You may wield 2 additional shields with your Psionic Field. Gain 1 strain to allow an ally to use one for a round.

features.name: Bladestorm (2)
features.text: You may wield 2-handed weapons with your Psionic Field, they are considered tri-wielded (1/round you may roll with advantage 2 with them).

subclasses.name: Adept of Illusions
subclasses.flavor: "Dual wielding, huh? Watch this!"

features.name: Figment
features.text: Reaction: when you Defend. You may gain 2 Strain to swap places with an enemy or willing ally within your Psionic Field, making them the new target.

features.name: Mirage
features.text:
1 action. +1 Strain/effect each round.
• **Danger.** Create an illusory danger in WIL contiguous spaces. Enemies who enter these spaces take 1d20+LVL psychic damage and must move out of the space before they can take any other action.

features.name: Mirage (2)
features.text:
Whenever you use Mirage, you may instead choose one of the following:
• **Disguise.** Project an illusory image into an enemy's mind (e.g., a wall, pit, or other obstacle or distraction). A lower level enemy gains your choice of Blinded, Taunted, or Prone. A creature your level or higher can make a WIL save to resist.
• **Distortion.** An ally gains your choice of Full Cover, Invisible, or becomes the source of Fear for their enemies.

features.name: Petrify!
features.text:
Trick a lower level enemy into thinking they are Petrified. A creature your level must make a WIL save?

Snap out of it! Illusions imposed upon an enemy end when the creature takes any damage.

subclasses.name: Adept of Collapse
subclasses.flavor: "Dual wielding, huh? Watch this!"

features.name: Mind Collapse
features.text:
Whenever you concentration ends, choose 2 Strain Dice, an enemy within Reach 3 suffers that damage instead of you (if no enemy is available, you take all of the damage as normal).

Remember! You can end concentration at any time on your turn for free.

features.name: Reverberating Mind
features.text: Double the Reach of Mind Collapse. Whenever any creature takes 10 or damage from your concentration breaking, the next time you create your Psionic Field this encounter, do so for free.

features.name: Mind Shield
features.text: When your concentration breaks, Taunt up to WIL creatures within Reach 6 for 1 round. You may Defend for free while Incapcitated. The first creature to attack you while Incapacitated also takes as much psychic damage.

features.name: Big Mind
features.text: Your Mind Collapse and Mind Shield have a Reach of 12. Choose up to 3 Strain Dice for Mind Collapse and 1 additional enemy to also suffer that damage.

faq.q: Alpha
faq.a: This is an early, alpha build of the class (it is not finished). Enough is here to test the main combat mechanics and get a feel for its style. Abilities will almost certainly be changed, many more will be added, others removed. If you have any feedback as you read it though and playtest it please let me know!

faq.q: Incapacitated?
faq.a: When your concentration breaks, you do not lose any actions but you cannot take any reactions that round (or other actions granted by an ally such as Coordinated Strike!), attacks have advantage against you, and any melee attack that hits, is turned into a crit.

faq.q: Psionic Blast
faq.a: You can use either KEY attribute. There is no attack roll, so this does not miss or crit, and is great as a 2nd or 3rd attack, vs minions, when Blinded, or otherwise Hampered.

classes.name: Revenant
classes.tagline: Neither living nor dead. Shrug off the afflictions of mere mortals as you embrace the line between life and death.
classes.flavor:
What it must be like, standing at the veil between life and death. Would one remember who they were before? I’ve only ever seen a Revenant once in my life. A noble warrior, his spirit clinging coldly to his body. His eyes, pale motionless pools of determination. His strikes slow, yet brutally powerful. I pity any warrior who crosses his path.

– Excerpt from a tattered journal.

A Revenant is bound to the mortal plane, driven by unfulfilled purpose, revenge, or perhaps even love. They exist on the razor’s edge between life and death, drawing upon the powers of the afterlife to fuel their undying might. Strike the Revenant down, and it rises again stronger and more determined than before.

features.name: Undying Might
features.text: While above 0 HP, add your max HP to all melee attacks you make. You have a max of 2 actions (while living and Dying).

features.name: Otherworldly Constitution
features.text: Whenever you roll a Hit Die to recover HP, you may instead recover that many Wounds (don't add your STR if you do this).

features.name: Spectral Form
features.text:
While Dying, you don't make STR saves to attack, and:
**Hate.** (Range 8) 1d8+WIL+Wounds (ignoring armor). Every 5th level deals +Wounds damage (e.g., at lvl 10 deal 1d8+WIL+(4xWounds).

features.name: Subclass
features.text: Choose a Revenant subclass.

features.name: Master of Undeath
features.text: Choose a Revenant Special Ability.

features.name: Key Stat Increase
features.text: +1 WIL or STR.

features.name: Secondary Stat Increase
features.text: +1 DEX or INT.

features.name: Death Grip
features.text: You may wield 2-handed weapons in 1 hand.

features.name: Incorporeal
features.text: Your Spectral Form gains: you cannot be Grappled/Restrained, and when you Defend, reduce damage to 0 instead.

features.name: Master of Undeath (2)
features.text: Choose a 2nd Revenant Special Ability.

features.name: Deadened Nerves
features.text: You cannot be crit while Dying (exploding dice are not rolled against you, ignore any “on crit” effects).

features.name: Subclass
features.text: Gain your Revenant subclass ability.

features.name: Key Stat Increase
features.text: +1 WIL or STR.

features.name: Deadened Nerves (2)
features.text: Reduce ALL damage taken by Wounds while living.

features.name: Master of Undeath (3)
features.text: Choose a 3rd Revenant Special Ability.

features.name: Secondary Stat Increase
features.text: +1 DEX or INT.

features.name: Incorporeal (2)
features.text: (1/encounter) Use Incorporeal ability while living.

features.name: Unrelenting as the Grave
features.text: Immune to Dazed, Fear, and effects that would move you or knock you Prone against your will.

features.name: Subclass
features.text: Gain your Revenant subclass ability.

features.name: Master of Undeath (4)
features.text: Choose a 4th Revenant Special Ability.

features.name: Key Stat Increase
features.text: +1 WIL or STR.

features.name: Secondary Stat Increase
features.text: +1 DEX or INT.

features.name: Master of Undeath (5)
features.text: Choose a 5th Revenant Special Ability.

features.name: Subclass
features.text: Gain your Revenant subclass ability.

features.name: Master of Undeath (6)
features.text: Choose a 6th Revenant Special Ability.

features.name: Key Stat Increase
features.text: +1 WIL or STR.

features.name: Secondary Stat Increase
features.text: +1 DEX or INT

features.name: Deadened Nerves (3)
features.text: Reduce ALL damage taken by 2x Wounds.

features.name: Spectral Power
features.text: (WIL/Safe Rest) You may use an ability from your living or Spectral Form without needing to be in that form.

features.name: Epic Boon
features.text: Choose an Epic Boon (see pg. 23 of the GM's Guide).

features.name: Two, as One
features.text: +1 to any 2 of your stats. You can use all Spectral Form abilities while living.

sidebars.title: At a Glance
sidebars.text:
Slow, but strong. Draw upon your undying might , taking fewer, but more powerful actions in battle.

Face your foes as both a powerful fighter and a wrathful spirit. Become a spectral wraith and unleash deathly powers.

Command fear in the hearts of your foes and bolster the will of your allies.

sidebars.title: Flavor is free!
sidebars.text: What is the your spectral form? Your own stubborn will? An evil possessing creature? Something you’ve made a bargain with? An ancestor or other friendly being? It’s up to you!

options.name: Ghost Step
options.text: While in Spectral Form, allies you move through may move with you (as long as they end their movement in an unoccupied space).

options.name: Patient as Death
options.text: Next turn, double your damage and number of targets for your attacks.

options.name: Innervating Spirit
options.text: While in Wraith Form, Dying allies also have a max of 2 actions.

options.name: Deathly Wail
options.text: When you drop to 0 HP, use Hate immediately for free against the attacker or against all others within Reach 2.

options.name: Possess
options.text: You may move through enemy spaces while Dying, you may force lower level enemies to follow you as you move (as long as they end their movement in an unoccupied space).

options.name: Spook
options.text: Frighten lower level enemies within Reach 8 When you move through an enemy space, they are Frightened this round.

options.name: Grips of Fear
options.text: Deal extra damage/Restrain to frightened enemies.

options.name: Iron Will
options.text: If you would miss an attack but haven’t dealt damage this round yet, reroll the attack (once).

options.name: Spiritshift
options.text: Whenever you drop to 0 HP you may teleport up to twice your speed away.

options.name: Strong Ties
options.text: Whenever you spend Hit Dice to recover HP, you may also heal a number of Wound equal to the number of dice rolled. If Dying when combat ends, recover 1 HP.

options.name: Deathwalk
options.text: On your turn, you may drop to 0 HP at will without taking a Wound. Any remaining HP are treated as Temp HP.

options.name: My Body, a Puppet
options.text: Your unliving corpse follows you and Interposes for you for free 1/ Round.

options.name: Haunt
options.text: Reaction: When damaged while Dying, spend an action for the attacker.

options.name: Possess
options.text: Gain 1 Wound to possess an adjacent ally until the start of your next turn, add your Max HP as damage to their attacks. You also take any damage they take.

options.name: Usurp
options.text: Move into the space of an enemy, you may gain 1 Wound to choose its actions during its next turn. Gain 2 Wounds instead if it is your level or higher.

ancestries.name: Human
ancestries.flavor: Found in every terrain and environment, their curiosity and ambition drive them to explore every corner of the world, making them a ubiquitous and versatile race.

traits.name: Tenacious
traits.text: +1 to all skills and Initiative.

ancestries.name: Dwarf
ancestries.flavor: Dwarf, in the old language, means “stone.” You are resilient, solid, stout. Even when driven to exhaustion, you will not falter. Forgoing speed, you are gifted with physical vitality and a belly that can handle the finest (and worst) consumables this world has to offer.

traits.name: Stout
traits.text: +2 max Hit Dice, +1 max Wounds, –1 Speed. You know Dwarvish if your INT isn’t negative.

ancestries.name: Elf
ancestries.flavor: Elves epitomize swiftness and grace. Their tall, slender forms belie their innate speed, grace, and wit. Formidable in both diplomacy and combat, elves strike swiftly, often preventing the worst by acting first.

traits.name: Lithe
traits.text: Advantage on Initiative, +1 Speed. You know Elvish if your INT isn’t negative.

ancestries.name: Halfling
ancestries.flavor: Kind of like a human, but smaller (except for the feet). Where does our luck come from? Well… you know what they say about rabbit feet? Well, we’ve got feet for days compared to them. Imagine the amount of luck you could fit into these bad boys!

traits.name: Elusive
traits.text: +1 to Stealth. (1/Safe Rest) If you fail a save, you can succeed instead.

ancestries.name: Gnome
ancestries.flavor: Eccentric, curious, and perpetually optimistic, gnomes are cheerful—especially when compared to their typically grumpier and larger kin, the dwarves. Known for their tinkering, spreading cheer, and playful antics, gnomes pursue their passions with a scatterbrained enthusiasm.

traits.name: Optimistic
traits.text: (Free Reaction, Reach 6) Allow an ally to reroll any 1 die; resets when healed to max HP. –1 Speed. You know Dwarvish if your INT isn’t negative (but you call it Gnomish, of course).

ancestries.name: Dragonborn
ancestries.flavor: The soul of a dragon burns within you, the scales of your body are like forged steel. You are a kiln and your heritage the coals that stoke your flames. Call upon your wrath to speak in the tongue of your ancestors and imbue unbridled fury into your attacks.

traits.name: Draconic Heritage
traits.text: +1 Defense. (1/Safe Rest) Deal an additional LVL+KEY damage on an attack divided as you choose among any of the attack’s targets (recharges whenever you gain a Wound). You know Draconic if your INT isn’t negative.

ancestries.name: Goblin
ancestries.flavor: Green, cunning, and perpetually vilified, Goblins thrive on the edge of chaos. For a Goblin, vanishing into the shadows is not just a skill—it’s an identity. After all, what kind of Goblin would you be if you couldn’t slip away unnoticed?

traits.name: Skedaddle
traits.text: Can move 2 spaces for free after you become the target of an attack or negative effect (after damage, ignoring Difficult Terrain). You know Goblin if your INT isn’t negative.

ancestries.name: Orc
ancestries.flavor: Just when you think you’ve bested a mighty Orc, you’ve merely succeeded in rousing their anger. Engaging in combat with an Orc is no endeavor for the weak-willed. While others may cower before death’s approach, Orcs boldly defy its grasp.

traits.name: Relentless
traits.text: (1/Safe Rest) When you would drop to 0 HP, you may set your HP to LVL instead. +1 Might. You know Goblin if your INT isn’t negative (but you call it Orcish, of course).

ancestries.name: Kobold
ancestries.flavor: Small, often maniacal, and dragon-obsessed. Kobolds thrive in familial groups, working together and finding ingenious ways to survive despite their diminutive size. Underestimated by many, Kobolds prove time and again that even the smallest among us can wield great power.

traits.name: Wily
traits.text: Advantage on skill checks related to dragons and to Influence friendly creatures. (1/encounter) Force an enemy to reroll a non-critical attack against you. You know Draconic if your INT isn’t negative.

ancestries.name: Fiendkin
ancestries.flavor: Said to have been born from a cursed bloodline or from the union of man and fiend, Fiendkin often find themselves outcasts in society. Yet, they embody determination in the face of adversity. Their ancestors didn’t emerge from the depths of the Everflame to succumb to minor setbacks!

traits.name: Flameborn
traits.text: 1 neutral save is advantaged instead. You know Infernal if your INT isn’t negative.

ancestries.name: Bunbun
ancestries.flavor: Bunbun are agile and unpredictable, using their powerful legs to leap great distances and catch foes off guard. Facing a Bunbun means contending with an opponent who can strike from unexpected angles and swiftly reposition themselves in the heat of battle.

traits.name: Bunny Legs
traits.text: (1/encounter) Before Interposing or after Defending (after damage), hop up to your Speed in any direction for free.

ancestries.name: Birdfolk
ancestries.flavor: Birdfolk find sanctuary not in stone or chains, but within the boundless expanse of the sky. However, the gift of flight comes at a cost—hollow bones, and commensurate frailty.

traits.name: Hollow Bones
traits.text: You can fly as long as you are wearing armor no heavier than Leather. Crits against you are Vicious (the attacker rolls 1 additional die).

ancestries.name: Celestial
ancestries.flavor: Descendants of divine beings, Celestials carry an aura of nobility and grace. Their innate connection to the higher planes allows them to resist the effects of misfortune, standing strong where others may falter.

traits.name: Highborn
traits.text: Your disadvantaged save is neutral instead. You know Celestial if your INT isn’t negative.

ancestries.name: Changeling
ancestries.flavor: Often hunted for their silver blood, Changelings are natural survivors, slipping into new identities with ease. Changelings that shift too often typically aren’t long for the world—they can struggle to remember who they once were, becoming little more than reflections of the faces they wear.

traits.name: New Place, New Face
traits.text: +2 Shifting Skill Points. You take on the appearance of any ancestry (transformation time 10 min). When you do, you may move your 2 Shifting Skill Points into any 1 skill.

ancestries.name: Crystalborn
ancestries.flavor: Formed from living crystal, the Crystalborn are beings of dazzling beauty and otherworldly toughness. Their translucent bodies refract light and sound, granting them unique abilities in combat.

traits.name: Reflective Aura
traits.text: (1/encounter) When you Defend, gain KEY Defense and deal KEY damage back to the attacker (ignoring their armor).

ancestries.name: Dryad/Shroomling
ancestries.flavor: Tied to the natural world, Dryads and Shroomlings embody the balance between flora and fauna. Their unique physiology releases toxic spores when harmed, providing a natural defense against those who dare to harm them.

traits.name: Danger Pollen/Spores
traits.text: Whenever you gain one or more Wounds, you excrete soporific spores: all adjacent enemies are Dazed. You know Elvish if your INT isn’t negative.

ancestries.name: Half-Giant
ancestries.flavor: Towering beings whose strength is as immovable as the mountains they call home. Their sheer size and resilience make them fearsome opponents, capable of surviving even devastating blows.

traits.name: Strength of Stone
traits.text: (1/encounter) Force an enemy to reroll a crit against you. +2 Might. You know Dwarvish if your INT isn’t negative (but you call it Giant, of course).

ancestries.name: Minotaur/Beastfolk
ancestries.flavor: Minotaur and other Beastfolk embody a primal connection to The Wild, combining strength with natural agility. Their powerful build allows them to move swiftly, whether repositioning to outflank foes or charging in with unstoppable force.

traits.name: Charge
traits.text: When you move at least 4 spaces, you can Knockback a creature in your path 1 space.

ancestries.name: Oozeling/Construct
ancestries.flavor: What even is a “PeOpLe” anyway? So what if your heart pumps oil instead of blood, so what if you don’t even have a heart!? If you can squish yourself into a pair of pants, or swing a sword like everyone else, who’s to say you can’t be a pEOpLe, too?!

traits.name: Odd Constitution
traits.text: Increment your Hit Dice one step (d6 » d8 » d10 » d12 » d20); they always heal you for the maximum amount. Magical healing always heals you for the minimum amount.

ancestries.name: Planarbeing
ancestries.flavor: You are not from this plane of existence—your soul is not as strongly tethered to it as others. But with this vulnerability comes power, the ability to temporarily shift from one plane to another in times of dire need.

traits.name: Planeshift
traits.text: –2 max Wounds. Whenever you Defend, you can gain 1 Wound to temporarily phase out of the material plane and ignore all effects of the attack.

ancestries.name: Ratfolk
ancestries.flavor: Ratfolk are survivors, thriving in the shadows of society where others fear to tread. Agile, resourceful, and fiercely loyal to their own, they have a knack for turning scraps into solutions.

traits.name: Scurry
traits.text: Gain +2 Defense if you moved on your last turn. +1 Speed.

ancestries.name: Stoatling
ancestries.flavor: Stoatlings may be small, but they’re far from weak. With fierce determination and warrior hearts, they can capably take down foes many times their size. Their agility and tenacity let them exploit larger enemies’ weaknesses, turning their size into a lethal advantage.

traits.name: Small But Ferocious
traits.text: Whenever you make a single-target attack against a creature larger than you, roll 1 additional d6 for each size category it is larger. They do the same.

ancestries.name: Turtle/Stonefolk
ancestries.flavor: Turtlefolk and Stonefolk take their time in everything they do; they are patient, sturdy, and slow to anger. They rely on their thick shells for protection, making them difficult to harm, but their cautious movements come at the cost of Speed.

traits.name: Slow & Steady
traits.text: +4 Defense, –2 Speed.

ancestries.name: Wyrdling
ancestries.flavor: Unpredictable and chaotic, Wyrdlings are the result of magic gone awry. Their bodies pulse with raw arcane energy, and their mere presence often disturbs the balance of magic around them.

traits.name: Chaotic Surge
traits.text: (1/encounter) Whenever you or a willing ally within Reach 6 casts a Tiered spell, you may allow them to roll on the Chaos Table.

backgrounds.name: Back Out of Retirement
backgrounds.text:
You’ve forgotten more than most adventurers these days know! Talk with your GM: what made you come out of retirement?
• Let’s see if I remember how to do this… Gain 1 Wound to use an ability or cast a spell as if you were 1 level higher.
• These old bones… Your age has long since started to show. –1 max Wounds.

backgrounds.name: Devoted Protector
backgrounds.text: Choose 1 ally in your party. You can survive +3 max Wounds as long as they are nearby. Whenever they take a Wound, you do too.

backgrounds.name: Academy Dropout
backgrounds.text: School just isn’t for everyone! You learn by experience in the real world (or at least that’s what you tell yourself). Learn any 1 Utility Spell.

backgrounds.name: Made a BAD Choice
backgrounds.text: Start with 500 or 1,000 extra gold, or an uncommon/rare magical item (that your GM allows). Gain an equally powerful curse or enemy who wants it back. If you choose this background, your GM may allow you to choose another.

backgrounds.name: Haunted Past
backgrounds.text: You are haunted by voices that occasionally give you cryptic advice. The voices are sometimes VERY helpful. Other times they only want to see you suffer. Advantage against fear.

backgrounds.name: Ear to the Ground
