backgrounds.text: Advantage on checks to know or obtain gossip for events that will soon happen or have happened less than 1 year ago.

backgrounds.name: What? I’ve Been Around
backgrounds.text:
(1/location; or at the GM’s discretion). You happen to know JUST the person who has the information you’re looking for, or could get you out of a jam, and… Roll 1d20:
• 1–5. They want you DEAD.
• 6–12. You owe them money.
• 13–19. They can be convinced to help you.
• 20. They are your biggest fan, or are madly in love with you.

backgrounds.name: Acrobat
backgrounds.text: Can be thrown by a larger ally, REALLY far. Resistant to falling and forced movement damage.

backgrounds.name: Wild One
backgrounds.text: Whether it is the sticks or flowers in your hair, your smell, or the way you carry yourself, wild creatures are less frightened of you and more willing to aid you. +1 Naturecraft. While Field Resting in the wild, your Hit Dice recover +KEY HP.

backgrounds.name: Fey Touched
backgrounds.text: You take half damage from all magical effects, double from weapons made of metal (before Defense is applied).

backgrounds.name: Survivalist
backgrounds.text: You never run out of your own personal rations. Anything can be food if you try hard enough! (1/Safe Rest) End poison on yourself. Advantage against poison saves. +1 max Hit Die.

backgrounds.name: Home at Sea
backgrounds.text: Recover twice as many Wounds and HP while Resting on a ship or near water. You can fill in for a first mate or captain in a pinch. Advantage on water-related skill checks.

backgrounds.name: At Home Underground
backgrounds.text: You can dig twice as fast as others. Safe Resting locations underground always count as Lavish lodging for you. You struggle to rest (INT save) while it’s raining. “Water… from the SKY?!”

backgrounds.name: Raised by Goblins
backgrounds.text: You speak Goblin natively (much better than one who has learned it later in life). You automatically notice and can avoid crudely made traps and have advantage to notice and disarm more sophisticated traps.

backgrounds.name: (Former) Con Artist
backgrounds.text: You can forge most documents or mimic voices flawlessly. You have a criminal contact in most major cities. However, your reputation often precedes you—until you prove yourself to be trustworthy.

backgrounds.name: History Buff
backgrounds.text: Advantage on all Lore checks about items, facts, or events that happened more than 100 years ago.

backgrounds.name: (Secretly) Undead
backgrounds.text: Unnatural Resilience: You are immune to disease and do not need to eat, drink, or breathe. Children, animals, and Celestials are uneasy in your presence; many will be horrified to discover your true nature.

backgrounds.name: Taste for the Finer Things
backgrounds.text: You always have up-to-date knowledge of the customs and dress of the upper classes and may even know many of their secrets. Advantage on Influence checks with the upper class.

backgrounds.name: Fearless
backgrounds.text: You are immune to being Frightened. +1 Initiative. –1 Defense.

backgrounds.name: So Dumb I’m Smart Sometimes
backgrounds.text: (2/Safe Rest) Reroll a failed INT-related skill or save with advantage.
backgrounds.requirement: Req. 0 or negative INT at character creation.

backgrounds.name: Wily Underdog
backgrounds.text: (2/Safe Rest) Reroll a failed STR attack, STR save, or Might check and use another stat instead.
backgrounds.requirement: Req. 0 or negative STR at character creation.

backgrounds.name: Bumblewise
backgrounds.text: A total of 1 or less on any WIL-related roll counts as a natural 20 (WIL save, Naturecraft, Perception, Influence, or Insight check).
backgrounds.requirement: Req. 0 or negative WIL at character creation.

backgrounds.name: Accidental Acrobat
backgrounds.text: Whenever you fail a DEX-related roll (e.g., DEX attack, DEX save, Stealth check, Finesse check), you may roll again. If you still fail, the consequences are BAD.
backgrounds.requirement: Req. 0 or negative DEX at character creation.

backgrounds.name: Tradesman/Artisan
backgrounds.text: Choose a profession (Baker/Cook, Smith, Stonemason, Weaver, Leatherworker, etc.). Checks you make related to that profession have advantage. You also retain special knowledge related to your profession.

motivations.name: I owe a life debt to someone in my party
motivations.text: Chat with your party: Who else needs help with their backstory? What did they do to help you?

motivations.name: I owe a LOT of money to some very dangerous people
motivations.text: What did you do with the money? Your GM probably has some GREAT ideas of bad guys you’re in deep with.

motivations.name: I need to grow in power to defeat someone who has wronged me
motivations.text: Do you know who wronged you, or are they unknown? Is it an individual or a larger group? Chat with your GM; they’ll love to help fill in the blanks.

motivations.name: I am searching for a way to bring a loved one (or someone I hate) back from the dead
motivations.text: Who even told you this was possible? What if they don’t remember you?

motivations.name: I am trying to get back home
motivations.text: Where is home for you? Do you even remember? What caused you to leave? Chat with your GM; they can give you some options of homelands.

motivations.name: I am searching for the one who stole something valuable from me
motivations.text: Is it an object? A person? A memory? Was it really stolen or did you make a bad bargain?

motivations.name: I was polymorphed into another kind of creature by a wizard
motivations.text: Hah! How would it feel for a cute halfling to become an ugly goblin? What did you do to anger the wizard?

motivations.name: Duty calls. I am honor-bound to serve
motivations.text: Who calls you? Your king? Your family? An ancient alliance or grudge? Talk with your GM and other players for ideas and mutual connections.

motivations.name: I was best friends with (and betrayed by) _______
motivations.text: Do you want to win them back? Get even? Warn others of their backstabbing? Talk with your GM about who this might be.

motivations.name: I’m lost
motivations.text: Physically? Emotionally? Spiritually? Are you in the wrong country or even plane of existence?

motivations.name: Wanderlust/Pilgrimage
motivations.text: What amazing thing do you want to see or experience? Have you spent too much time away from the road? Your GM probably has some fantastic locations in mind for you.

motivations.name: My hometown is in danger
motivations.text: Are you looking for a cure? Mercenaries? Personal strength?

motivations.name: Curiosity! I want to learn the DEEP secrets
motivations.text: Which secrets? Magical, lore, politics, what really happened in history?

motivations.name: To prove my worth
motivations.text: You were always underestimated—by your family, your village, your peers, or yourself. What will it take to show them you’re more than they thought? What kind of recognition do you seek?

motivations.name: I’m following a prophecy
motivations.text: A mysterious figure or ancient text foretold that you would play a crucial role in the fate of the world. What do you know of the prophecy? Do you believe it?

items.name: Healing Potions
items.text: Healing potions are deep, shimmering red elixirs with a refreshing, effervescent taste. These potions are crucial for quick recovery, though their availability is limited. Small towns may have only a few, while cities offer more (but they are not in unlimited supply). The wealthy often use them as a display of affluence, incorporating them into elaborate mixed drinks at social events to showcase their status. Potions require 1 action to drink or to administer to an adjacent willing creature.

items.name: Torches & Lanterns
items.text: Heroes can’t see in the dark, so they are Blind while fighting with no light. Heroes can bring a lantern or torch to light their way as long as they have a hand free (or some other way) to hold it. A torch typically lasts for 1 dungeon (or 1 level of a very large one). An oil lamp can typically last for 1 entire outing, until your next Safe Rest. Both cast light up to **6 spaces** away; beyond this is darkness.

items.name: Healing Potion
items.text: (action) Heal 2d4+4 HP.

items.name: Greater Healing Potion
items.text: (action) Heal 3d6+6 HP.

items.name: Supreme Healing Potion
items.text: (action) Heal 4d8+8 HP.

items.name: Torch (stack of 2)
items.text: For when it’s dark. 1 use each.

items.name: Lantern & Oil
items.text: Like a torch, but not as cool (refill: 1 gp).

items.name: Medical Kit (1 use)
items.text: Recover 1 Wound during a Field Rest.

items.name: Vial of Pitch
items.text: Sticky, and VERY flammable.

items.name: Rope (50 ft.)
items.text: You always need rope.

items.name: Chain (10 ft.)
items.text: Like rope, but stronger (and heavy).

items.name: Bucket
items.text: Also works as a hat in a pinch!

items.name: Padlock & Key
items.text: Lock it or lose it.

items.name: Mirror
items.text: For medusas AND spinach teeth.

items.name: Telescope
items.text: Arrr.

items.name: Magnifying Glass
items.text: Make the small, big.

items.name: Chalk
items.text: Not JUST for kids.

items.name: Shovel
items.text: Sometimes you need a hole dug.

items.name: Pulley
items.text: Pull down, go up.

items.name: Grappling Hook
items.text: For climbing or catching BIG fish.

items.name: Quiver & Ammo
items.text: Don’t leave home without it.

items.name: Saw
items.text: For cutting lumber.

items.name: Soap
items.text: Useless.

items.name: Strange Plant
items.text: Who knows?

items.name: Shiny Object
items.text: Worthless, but VERY pretty.

items.name: Lock Pick
items.text: It’s not mine, honest!

items.name: Bell
items.text: For service.

items.name: Dice
items.text: Math rocks. LOTS of fun.

items.name: Blanket
items.text: Warm & fuzzy.

items.name: Hunting Trap
items.text: Snap snap, don’t lose a finger!

items.name: Camping Supplies
items.text: Bedroll, rations, simple tent.

items.name: Crowbar
items.text: It’s LIKE a key.

items.name: Pitons
items.text: Metal spikes, for sealing doors.

items.name: Manacles
items.text: For when someone has been bad.

items.name: Instrument
items.text: Drums, Horn, Lyre, Flute, etc.

items.name: Large Sack
items.text: Like a BIG pocket.

items.name: Weapon of Many Hands
items.text: While equipped, this weapon grants the wielder additional arms. The wielder can use the extra arms to perform any task their normal hands can do (wield equipment, Grapple, climb, etc.) but they don’t let the wielder act any faster (and these extra appendages may be horrifying to people in polite society). A weapon that grants 1 extra hand is likely to be uncommon; 4 extra hands, legendary.

items.name: Harbinger & Sovereign, Abyssal’s Claim
items.text: Set of 2 matching glaives, +4 extra arms while both are equipped.

items.name: Weapon of Animosity
items.text: Whenever you attack with this weapon, roll an additional animosity die. The weapon deals that much additional damage to your target on a hit. Whenever this weapon misses, you take that damage instead. A weapon that adds 1d4 is likely to be uncommon; 1d10 or greater, legendary.

items.name: Weapon of Slaying
items.text: Whenever you attack with this weapon, it deals an additional die of damage against a particular creature type. Those creatures may try to kill you first. A 1d4 weapon of slaying is likely to be uncommon; 1d10 or more, legendary.

items.name: Gnatbane Weapon
items.text: Does not miss Small or Tiny creatures (they may hate you for it and attack you first).

items.name: Weapon of Wounding
items.text: When you land a hit with this weapon, you may suffer 1d6 damage to deal twice that much additional damage to your target.

items.name: Trinket of Ill Omen
items.text: While equipped, you have –1 to saves you roll and +1 to your save DC.

items.name: Mindlink Daggers
items.text: A matched pair of slender, silver daggers with intertwining runes. Enables the sharing of thoughts between any who hold (or are stabbed by) one.

items.name: Bloodstained Quill
items.text: If you dip this quill into the blood of a dead intelligent creature, the quill animates and writes the last words spoken by that creature.

items.name: Eyes of the Street
items.text: A pair of goggles covered in muck that you can’t ever clean off completely. While wearing them, you can look at a rat or a pigeon to gain the ability to see and hear through its senses for 10 minutes. Once you use this ability, you must whisper a secret to the goggles before you can use them again. That secret always seems to become a local rumor before too long…

items.name: Handwraps of Force
items.text: While wearing these wraps, whenever you make an Unarmed Strike, you may Knockback your target up to 2 spaces and yourself the same distance in the opposite direction. You may instead make an attack with no target, striking the air to propel yourself 4 spaces in any direction.

items.name: Resolute Fangs, Golden Bastion
items.text: +8 Defense. Whenever you reduce damage from a melee attack with this shield, it may Grapple the attacker regardless of its size (escape DC 20 STR, max 1 creature). Action: Speak this shield’s command word to make it immovable, fixed in place, until it is spoken again.

items.name: Key of Doors
items.text: Insert this key into any locked door to open it, not to the room beyond, but to any doorway you’ve previously walked through while holding this item.

items.name: Grim Coronet
items.text: When you would die while wearing this crown, gain 3 actions and take a turn immediately. You die at the end of your turn.

items.name: Vindication
items.text: A jagged blade marred by scorch marks and dark stains, radiating a bitter, vengeful energy that punishes both wielder and foe alike. +1d12 damage. You take this damage on a miss.

items.name: Pocket Cauldron
items.text:
While Safe Resting, use this to brew your choice of 1 potion, to be consumed immediately:
• **Elixir of Futuresight:** This potion grants the drinker a brief, cryptic vision of a future event.
• **Elixir of Requiem:** This potion allows the drinker to relive a crucial memory from their past.
• **Elixir of Time:** Once every 100 years, the cauldron can brew a potion that can take the drinker back in time 1 day.

items.name: Phoenix Helm
items.text: If you die while wearing this golden helm, your body explodes in flames and hot ash. You rise anew from the ashes… (see pg. 71 of the Game Master’s Guide for more).

items.name: Ball of Spiders
items.text: A black, palm-sized ball with faintly writhing patterns etched into its surface. **Action:** Throw this ball up to 6 spaces. Upon impact, it shatters, releasing a swarm of harmless but horrifyingly realistic spectral spiders that cover a 2×2 area. Creatures in the area must make a WIL save or be Frightened until the end of their next turn. Once used, the ball reforms at the next Safe Rest.

items.name: Skitter Shoes
items.text: While wearing these shoes, you can walk on vertical surfaces or ceilings as if they were flat ground, but only at half Speed. If you end your turn upside down or on a vertical surface, you must make a DC 10 STR save or fall down, landing Prone.

items.name: Button of Protection
items.text:
A small, unassuming button etched with a faintly glowing sigil. When sewn onto an outfit, as a reaction when you are attacked, you may pull the button off and throw it into the air. The button emits a sudden, dazzling flash of light and a high-pitched whistle. The attacker must make a WIL save or be Distracted, causing the attack to miss you.

After use, the button becomes inert. It can be sewn back onto a garment during a Safe Rest by an experienced seamstress or tailor with silver thread, which reactivates its power.

items.name: Wand of Fire Step
items.text: **Recharge:** Heat the wand in a blacksmith’s forge until it glows, then quench it in oil.

items.name: Wand of Dread Visage
items.text: **Recharge:** Place the wand in a freshly slain corpse. Leave it until only bones remain.

items.name: Wand of Fly
items.text: **Recharge:** Give it to a wild bird and let it fly freely. Retrieve it wherever the bird drops it.

items.name: Wand of Glacier Strike
items.text: **Recharge:** Leave the wand at the bottom of a lake until it freezes over and thaws naturally.

items.name: Wand of Ride the Lightning
items.text: **Recharge:** Place at the highest point within 1 mile. Retrieve after 3 thunderstorms.

items.name: Wand of Barrier of Wind
items.text: **Recharge:** Hang the wand with wind chimes in a breezy area. Let it ring for 3 days.

items.name: Wand of Sacrifice
items.text: **Recharge:** Plant it in a new garden. Leave it undisturbed until the flowers bloom.

items.name: Elderwyrm’s Majesty
items.text:
This wand can cast Dragonform, turning into the type of dragon that last charged it.
**Recharge:** Give an ancient dragon a gift that it truly desires.

items.name: Heartwood, Splinter of the Tree of Life
items.text:
Cast Redeem with no required components.
**Recharge:** A sacred hymn must be sung over it ceaselessly for 100 years.

items.name: Gem of Escape
items.text: These magical gems are always crafted in pairs and can have any number of willing creatures magically bound to them. Crush one (1 Action) in case of emergency to instantly teleport ALL who are bound to it to the location of the other gem.

items.name: Glacier in a Bottle
items.text: When poured out (1 Action), it creates a solid form of ice, filling any number of unoccupied consecutive spaces up to 6 spaces away and 2 spaces high. The ice lasts for 1 hour before melting. Extreme heat or damage may cause it to fail prematurely. 1/Safe Rest.

items.name: Phoenix Helm
items.text:
On Death: You are reborn as a golden fiery phoenix. Enemies within 6 spaces take **LVL d10** fire damage on a failed **DC 10+KEY** DEX save (half on save). Gain the following stats and abilities:
• Gain a fly Speed and Defense of 10 and 10×LVL HP.
• Creatures that touch you take LVL fire damage.
• **Fiery Talons.** 1 Action, 1d10+LVL damage.
After 10 minutes, this form ends, the helm is no more and you return with 0 HP and all but 1 Wound.

items.name: The Grimoire of Truths
items.text: This sentient magical book possesses an extensive knowledge of the world, past events, people’s motivations, and even possible future outcomes. It eagerly converses with its owner, presenting itself as a helpful companion. However, its true goal is to gain their trust, offering just enough useful insight to ultimately lead them into great trouble.
items.flavor:
“Ah, another mortal thirsting for knowledge.”
“Power comes at a cost. But then, so does ignorance.”
“Oh, **that one**? Her smile hides a thousand lies and treacheries.”
“Would you like the safe, **boring** route, or the one filled with **excitement** and potential doom? I know which one I’d pick.”

items.name: Hear-ring
items.text: A simple piece of jewelry worn on the ear. While worn, wearers can communicate with one another no matter the distance. Frequently crafted as a pair, sometimes as a larger set.

items.name: Pocket Cauldron
items.text:
While taking a Safe Rest, use this cauldron to brew a single potion of your choice, which must be consumed immediately:
• **Elixir of Futuresight:** Grants the drinker a brief, cryptic vision of a future event.
• **Elixir of Requiem:** Allows the drinker to relive a crucial memory from their past.
• **Elixir of Time:** Once every 100 years, the cauldron can brew a potion that can take the drinker back in time 1 day.

items.name: Lumina, Living Sunbeam
items.text: A small, radiant orb of light, about the size of an apple, with a gentle, warm glow that pulses with life and a perpetually cheerful expression. She is a one-time-use item that, when activated as an action, will deal **LVL d6** radiant damage to all enemies within Reach 6 and heal allies in the area for the same amount. Until then, she hovers around her owner, spreading warmth and light, and offering encouragement.
items.flavor: “I’m here to brighten your journey! And, when the time comes, it’s okay… don’t be afraid to let me shine.” —Lumina

properties.name: 2-handed
properties.text: Can be held in a single hand, but must be wielded in 2 hands to attack with it.

properties.name: Load
properties.text: Some weapons require extra actions to load before each shot.

properties.name: Reach
properties.text: How close an enemy must be to be affected by this attack. If unspecified, Reach 1.

properties.name: Range
properties.text: Attacks can be made from afar. If any enemy is adjacent to you, your Ranged attacks have disadvantage. Add 1 die of disadvantage to gain +2 Range (max +6 additional Range; disadvantage 3).

properties.name: Thrown
properties.text: Treat a melee weapon as if it had Range. Once thrown, you no longer have it!

properties.name: Vicious
properties.text: Roll 1 additional die whenever you roll crit damage.

spells.name: Revive
spells.text: Bring a dead creature back to life, provided they’ve been dead no more than 10 days and have not been revived by this spell before. Attempting to revive a creature already brought back with this spell risks raising a mindless, zombified husk instead.

spells.name: Sparkfetch
spells.text: Loudly teleport a tiny, unheld metal item you can see to yourself.

spells.name: Lesser Windform
spells.text: You are Invisible and Blind for the duration of the spell.

spells.name: Greater Windform
spells.text: Gain Invisibility, a fly speed of 10, and the ability to slip through any space that wind can pass through.

spells.name: Fly
spells.text: Reach: 1. Concentration: Up to 10 min. Grant a creature a flying Speed. They can move KEY spaces for free on their turn.

spells.name: Radiant Bond
spells.text: Telepathically communicate across any distance with a creature that holds a gift you have freely given.

spells.name: Speak With Dead
spells.text: Temporarily animate a corpse, allowing it to answer up to 3 questions before returning to rest. The corpse must answer, but it isn’t required to be truthful if it dislikes the questioner or the questions.

spells.name: Hearth & Home
spells.text: Conjure a welcoming inn, complete with sturdy wooden tables, plush chairs, and a soft rug underfoot. At its heart burns a cozy fire in a fireplace, filling the space with warmth and light. The inn lasts for 12 hours and vanishes without a trace afterward.

spells.name: Teleport
spells.text: You and up to 10 willing creatures within 2 spaces are instantly teleported to a place of your choice that you have visited before.

spells.name: Cryotomb
spells.text: Range: 12. A target must make a STR save or become Incapacitated in an icy tomb and immune to harm. This lasts as long as you remain alive, or until the ice melts or is otherwise destroyed. The creature may repeat the save once every 10 days. Huge or larger creatures have advantage on the save. Small or Tiny creatures have disadvantage.

spells.name: Memory Veil
spells.concentration: as long as the caster remains conscious.
spells.text: Conceal or change all memories of an event for up to 12 creatures within 2 spaces on a failed WIL save for as long as this spell lasts.

spells.name: Flame Dart
spells.text: Range: 10. Damage: 1d10. On crit: Smoldering.

spells.name: Heart’s Fire
spells.text: Range: 4. (1/round) Give an ally 1 action. Cast as a Reaction for 1 mana.

spells.name: Ignite
spells.text: Range: 10. Damage: 4d10 to a Smoldering target.

spells.name: Enchant Weapon
spells.text: Concentration: 1 min. Reach: 8. A weapon you choose inflicts Smoldering on crit and gains (1/turn) +KEY damage.

spells.name: Flame Barrier
spells.text:
Castable only while Defending.
Reach: 1, AoE. Damage: 10+KEY and Smoldering. Triggers whenever you are attacked this round.

spells.name: Pyroclasm
spells.text: Reach: 3, AoE. Damage: 2d20+10, half on DEX save (Smoldering creatures fail).

spells.name: Fiery Embrace
spells.text: Concentration: 1 min. Reach: 10, AoE. An ally gains the effects of Enchant Weapon. Enemies gain Smoldering, and effects that would end it, don’t.

spells.name: Living Inferno
spells.text: Gain the effects of Flame Barrier until your next turn. At the end of this turn and your next turn, cast Pyroclasm for free.

spells.name: Dragonform
spells.text:
Transform into a Huge dragon. Gain 3 actions, a flying Speed of 12, LVL Defense, 10×LVL temp HP, and:
• Tooth & Claw. 1 Action: (Reach 2) 1d20+LVL damage (ignoring armor). Inflicts Smoldering.
• Immolating Breath. 2 Actions: (Cone 10, AoE) KEY d20 damage, half on DEX save (Smoldering targets fail).
Note. You can maintain this form for as long as the temp HP granted by this spell remain (max. 10 min). When it ends, you drop to 0 HP.

spells.name: Ice Lance
spells.text: Range: 12. Damage: 1d6 cold/piercing, Slowed.

spells.name: Snowblind
spells.text: Reach: 1. Damage: 1d6, Blind until the end of their next turn.

spells.name: Frost Shield
spells.text:
Castable only while Defending.
Gain 2×KEY temp HP until the start of your next turn.

spells.name: Shatter
spells.text: Range: 12. Damage: 3d6. ANY die can crit vs a Hampered target. On crit: +20 damage (instead of rolling any additional dice).
spells.higherLevels: Increase a die roll by 1 and +5 damage on crit.

spells.name: Omenrime
spells.text:
Reach: 6. Roll 1d6; you may replace any single die rolled within Reach with that die (it expires at the end of the encounter if unused).
Replacing a die. Swap the die for your d6; treat it as if that die were the original roll.

spells.name: Rimeblades
spells.text: Concentration: 1 min. Reach: 12, AoE. Conjure icy blades in 5 contiguous spaces; this area is Difficult Terrain. Creatures there (or who enter later) suffer 2d6 damage for each space they touch.

spells.name: Arctic Blast
spells.text: Reach: Cone 4, AoE. Damage: 4d6+10. This area is Difficult Terrain for 1 round. Any already Hampered creatures there are Restrained (frozen in place).

spells.name: Glacier Strike
spells.text: Range: 12, 3×3 AoE. Damage: d66 bludgeoning. Creatures adjacent to that area take half as much. The entire area permanently becomes Difficult Terrain.

spells.name: Arctic Annihilation
spells.text:
Reach: 12, AoE. Any targets you choose are encased in ice and immune to damage and negative effects until the start of their next turn. All others take d66 damage, then make a STR save or be Incapacitated until the end of their next turn.
Note. Once you cast this spell, you must Safe Rest for 1 week before using it again.

spells.name: Zap
spells.text: Range: 8. Damage: 1d8+4. On miss: you take half the damage instead.

spells.name: Overload
spells.text:
Castable only if Charged, ending the condition.
Reach: 2, AoE. Damage: 2d8.

spells.name: Arc Lightning
spells.text:
Range: 12. Damage: 3d8. Also hits the next closest creature.
Next Closest Creature. If you are the closest, you are hit! If 2 creatures are equally close, the GM can select randomly, the taller one, or whoever has the most metal.

spells.name: Alacrity
spells.text: (1/turn) Teleport up to your Speed, gain Charged (can be cast while Defending, after damage).

spells.name: Stormlash
spells.text: Line: 12, AoE. Damage: 3d8+4 and Prone on a failed STR save. Creatures with a large amount of metal (e.g., armor or a longsword) roll with disadvantage and suffer +10 damage.

spells.name: Electrickery
spells.text:
Castable when an ally is attacked.
Range: 8. Teleport an ally away. Teleport another creature there on a failed WIL save (making them the target). Costs 1 action if Charged, ending the condition.

spells.name: Electrocharge
spells.text: Concentration: 1 min. Reach: 4. Give a creature Charged, +1 max action, +5 Defense, 2× Speed, and advantage on DEX saves.

spells.name: Ride the Lightning
spells.text: Reach: 12, AoE. Teleport to a spot you can see (if a willing creature is there, swap places with them). Adjacent creatures take d88 damage and Knockback 2. Creatures moved 2+ spaces are also knocked Prone, Dazed, and deafened for 1 day.

spells.name: Seething Storm
spells.text:
Concentration: 1 min. Become a cloud of tempestuous storm. You can fly, move for free 1/round, and attacks against you are disadvantaged. At the end of each of your turns, strike up to 4 creatures within Reach 4 with a bolt of lightning for d88 damage (a creature can only be struck 1/round).
Costs 3 actions each round to maintain. +2 Reach and +2 lightning bolts each round.
Note. Once you cast this spell, you must Safe Rest for 1 week before you can use it again.

spells.name: Razor Wind
spells.text: Range: 12. Damage: 2d4 slashing, with advantage OR include a 2nd creature adjacent to your target.

spells.name: Breath of Life
spells.text: Range: 6. Restore 1d4 HP to a Dying creature. If healed for 4+: they also regain 1 action.

spells.name: Blustery Gale
spells.text: Range: 12. Damage: 3d4 bludgeoning (advantage vs flying/Small/Tiny). Hit or miss, Knockback 2.

spells.name: Barrier of Wind
spells.text:
Castable only while Defending vs Ranged.
Reduce the Primary Die by 3. If it misses, redirect the original attack to another space within Reach 1.

spells.name: Echoburst
spells.text: Reach: 1. Damage: d44 bludgeoning (ignoring armor). Any creature in the targeted space at the beginning of your next turn takes this damage again.

spells.name: Eye of the Storm
spells.text: Reach: 3, AoE. Damage: 4d4+10 bludgeoning to enemies. Place surviving creatures anywhere within 1 space of the storm’s Reach on a failed STR save.

spells.name: Updraft
spells.text: Reach: 12, 5×5 AoE. Damage: 20 bludgeoning minus a DEX save. On 10+ damage, they land Prone and Dazed.

spells.name: Thousand Cuts
spells.text: Range: 12. Damage: d44 slashing with advantage. Also damages enemies within Reach 1 of your target.

spells.name: Boisterous Winds
spells.text: Reach: 12. Gently move all creatures up to 6 spaces, each in a straight line in a direction of your choice. At the beginning of your subsequent turns, do so again but 2 fewer spaces.

spells.name: Rebuke
spells.text: Reach: 4. Damage: 1d8 (ignoring armor). 2× damage against undead or cowardly (those Frightened or behind Cover).

spells.name: True Strike
spells.text: Reach: 4. A target gains advantage (ignoring all sources of disadvantage) and +1 Reach on their next attack this encounter.

spells.name: Heal
spells.text:
Reach: 1. Heal a target 1d8+KEY HP.
Powerful Healing. If 5+ mana is spent, heal a negative condition as well (e.g., Blind, 1 Wound).

spells.name: Warding Bond
spells.text: Concentration: 1 min. Reach: 4. Make an ally your ward: they take 2 less damage from all sources. (1/round) When they are attacked, you may be attacked for some or all of the damage instead.

spells.name: Condemn
spells.text:
Vs enemies who have crit since you last damaged them.
Reach: 4. Damage: 30. Cannot be reduced by any means. The next attack against that enemy gains advantage.

spells.name: Shield of Justice
spells.text:
Castable only while Defending.
Creatures who attack you are Blinded (until the end of their next turn); you deal damage back to each (ignoring armor) equal to damage you take this round.

spells.name: Vengeance
spells.text:
Can only target enemies who attacked a Dying ally or reduced one to 0 HP since your last turn.
Reach: 1. Damage: 1d100.

spells.name: Sacrifice
spells.text:
Reach: 4. Reduce yourself to 0 HP and you cannot have more than 0 HP until you Safe Rest. Heal HP equal to your max HP, divided as you choose among any other creatures.
Dead? You may revive a creature that has died in the past minute if you give them at least 20 HP (also healing 2 Wounds from them), provided they have not been revived with this spell before.

spells.name: Celestial Legion
spells.text:
(1/turn) Any friendly creature may use 1 of 3 charges to call upon higher powers for aid this encounter:
• Reckoning. When you attack, gain advantage (ignoring all disadvantage) and add 1d20 damage to the attack; with advantage too, if Bloodied.
• Trembling. When attacked, the enemy becomes Frightened of you until the end of their next turn. Reduce the incoming damage by 1d20 if Bloodied.

spells.name: Redeem
spells.text:
Requires (and consumes) a diamond worth 10,000 gp.
Reach: 1 mile. Revive any number of creatures that have died in the past year, provided they have not died of old age or been revived with this spell before.

spells.name: Entice
spells.text: (1/round) Range: 12. Damage: 1d12 (ignoring armor). Target moves Primary Die spaces closer to you and gains 1d12 on their next attack.
spells.cantripScaling: You may add 1d12 to both every 5th level.

spells.name: Withering Touch
spells.text: Reach: 1. Damage: 1d12. On damage, target is considered undead for 1 round.

spells.name: Shadow Trap
spells.text:
Reaction: When an enemy moves next to an ally within Reach 8.
Damage: 2d12. If Small/Tiny, the enemy is also Restrained until they escape.
spells.higherLevels: +1 size category and +1d12 damage on escape.

spells.name: Dread Visage
spells.text:
Castable only while Defending.
Damage: 1d12 and Frighten all creatures attacking you in melee this round. Costs 2 mana less while Dying.

spells.name: Vampiric Greed
spells.text: Reach: 1, AoE. Damage: 4d12. Heal HP equal to the damage dealt then gain 1 Wound. Gain 1 additional Wound for each creature that survived this damage.

spells.name: Vigor Mortis
spells.text:
Castable only when an ally drops to 0 HP.
Concentration: 1 min. Reach: 8. Their max actions do not change, they skip STR saves to act, and taking damage while Dying causes 1 fewer Wound (min 1).

spells.name: Gangrenous Burst
spells.text: Reach: Up to 8, AoE. Damage: 3d20 (ignoring armor) to damaged creatures, half on STR save (targets have disadvantage if Bloodied).

spells.name: Unspeakable Word
spells.text: Reach: 8. Damage: d66 with advantage (ignoring armor). On a failed INT save (disadvantage if Bloodied or Frightened) the target is Weakened 10, and you are Empowered 10 on your next attack. On save, the opposite happens instead.

spells.name: Creeping Death
spells.text: Reach: 8, AoE. Damage: 4d20. If this kills the creature, repeat the damage to another creature within Reach 8 of it not yet damaged by this effect. Repeat until a target survives or no others are within Reach.

spells.name: Firebrand
spells.text: Touch a surface and secretly mark it with a symbol or brief message. Speaking a chosen command word while nearby reveals it.

spells.name: Fire Step
spells.text: Teleport to a fire source you can see.

spells.name: Kindle
spells.text: Conjure a minor visual illusion. OR: Ignite a small, unheld item within Reach 6.

spells.name: Chillcraft
spells.text:
Chill. Harmlessly freeze, thaw, or move a bath-sized amount of water near you. OR:
Craft. Conjure a sheet of opaque, mirror-like, or transparent ice the size of a window or door.

spells.name: Ice Disk
spells.text: Conjure a floating disk of ice that follows you. It can carry moderately heavy weight for 1 hour or until you cast this spell again.

spells.name: Wintry Scrying
spells.text: Turn a small patch of water into a reflective icy mirror. Looking through it grants you vision of any desired location near this body of water for 10 min.

spells.name: Spark Buddy
spells.text: Conjure a Tiny (squirrel-sized) helper for up to 1 hour. It can fetch Tiny objects, open unlocked doors, illuminate a small area, or deliver a harmless shock. If it takes damage or moves further than 6 spaces away from you, it dissipates into sparks.

spells.name: Spark Step
spells.text: Reach: 4. Teleport to a metal object.

spells.name: Tempest’s Command
spells.text: Dispel a minor magical effect, or temporarily suppress a stronger one (the more powerful an enchantment, the shorter the duration). OR: Your eyes glow and your voice is amplified to a thunder-like volume for 1 min.

spells.name: Wind Whisper
spells.text: You whisper a message into the wind and it will be secretly carried to a specified target anywhere wind could reach.

spells.name: Helpful Gust
spells.text: Reach: 6. Gently move a Tiny unheld item in any direction. OR: Generate an illusory scent.

spells.name: Feather Fall
spells.text: Reach: 6. Reaction: When a creature falls, cause them to gently float to the ground.

spells.name: Light
spells.text: Cause an item to brightly glow as a torch with radiant light for as long as you hold it.

spells.name: Beautify
spells.text: Clean stains or repair a small tear/break in a non-magical item, or conjure tiny beautiful things: flowers, butterflies, etc.

spells.name: Bond of Peace
spells.text:
Bond. Telepathically communicate simple thoughts or feelings with a friendly creature you can see. OR:
Peace. Imbue your spoken words with calming magic, granting advantage on any check made to soothe anger or fear in creatures who can hear you.

spells.name: Gravecraft
spells.text:
Gravemark. Magically soil a surface with blood, filth, or other disgusting things (1 Action).
Gravework. Shape/move a body-sized plot of earth (1 Minute).

spells.name: False Face
spells.text: Change your appearance to look like someone else for 10 min. Requires a piece of them.

spells.name: Thought Leech
spells.text: Reach: 6. Read the surface thoughts of a creature. They can sense you doing this and may not like it.

spells.name: Summon Shadow
spells.text:
Summon 1 adjacent Shadow (a d12 minion).

Minions. They follow the minion rules and abandon you immediately outside of combat.
Shadow Limit. You can have up to INT Shadows.

spells.name: Command Shadows
spells.text: ALL your Shadows move 6 then attack (1/round).

spells.name: Shadow Blast
spells.text: Range: 8. Damage: 1d12+DEX (1/round).

spells.name: Lifebinding Spirit
spells.text:
Summon a spirit companion (max 1) that follows you and is immune to harm. It can act upon a target within Reach 4 of you before returning to your side. It can:
• **Harm.** 1 Action: It attacks for 1d8+STR radiant damage (ignoring Armor).
• **Mend.** 1 Action: (WIL/Safe Rest) It restores WIL d20 HP to a Dying creature.

spells.name: Vicious Mockery
spells.text: Range: 12. Damage: 1d6+INT psychic (ignoring Armor). On hit: target is Taunted until the end of their next turn.

spells.name: Misery
spells.text: Reach: 8. Damage: 1d8+LVL. On hit: apply an Affliction. On crit: apply 2 instead.

spells.name: Life Bloom
spells.text: Reach: 8. You and a willing target each spend 1 Hit Die. Your target and another creature within Reach each heal 10 HP.

spells.name: Twitch Curse
spells.text:
Castable only while Defending.
Reach: 8. First, move the attacker 1 space (+1 for each Affliction on it). Opportunity Attacks this triggers have advantage instead of disadvantage.
Note. If you are no longer a valid target (e.g., the attacker is dead, you are out of line of sight/Reach/Range), the triggering attack misses.

spells.name: Bloodcurse
spells.text: Reach: 8. Damage: 1d4+LVL (increment the die size for each Affliction it has). On hit: the target becomes secretly Bloodcursed, suffering the same damage it deals next (ignoring armor).

spells.name: Wyrding Strands
spells.text: Reach: 8. Move creatures within Reach a total of 2d6 spaces, divided among them as you choose.

spells.name: Frogify
spells.text: Reach: 8. (1/encounter) Turn a Medium or smaller creature into a harmless frog until the end of its next turn. Make it hop immediately up to KEY spaces, and again on its turn instead of acting. The first attack against it crits and ends the effect.

spells.name: Malediction
spells.text: Reach: 4. Up to KEY creatures of your choice take 1d8+LVL damage (ignoring armor).

spells.name: Circle of Thorns
spells.text: Reach: 8. Ward every space adjacent to a creature with magical thorns. Enemies that enter a warded space take LVL damage and are Weakened 10 until the end of their next turn. Lasts 1 min or until it has triggered KEY times.

spells.name: Terror
spells.text:
Reach: 8. Damage: 1d6 (ignoring armor); roll with advantage for each Affliction on the target; multiply the result by LVL.
Example. If a target has 1 Affliction, roll 2d6 and keep the highest, then if you are level 10 multiply the highest die by 10.

boons.name: Aggressive
boons.text: On your first round of combat you can spend 1 Action from your next turn.

boons.name: Ancestry Trait
boons.text: Select another Ancestry trait (provided it makes sense).

boons.name: Brave
boons.text: +2 to damage while you have the most enemies adjacent to you.

boons.name: Good Patient
boons.text: Whenever you would receive healing, you heal an additional KEY HP.

boons.name: Hardy
boons.text: Whenever you increase your max HP, roll with advantage 2 instead.

boons.name: Honorable Protector
boons.text: Gain LVL temp HP whenever you Interpose. Suffer LVL psychic damage whenever an ally within 2 spaces is attacked and you don’t Interpose.

boons.name: Lionhearted
boons.text: +2 Defense while you have the most enemies adjacent to you.

boons.name: Resilient
boons.text: (1/Safe Rest) You are immune to Wounds this turn.

boons.name: Resolute
boons.text: When pushed, you are pushed 1 space less. Whenever you would be knocked Prone, you can instead be moved back 1 space. 1/turn.

boons.name: Smart, Not Book Smart
boons.text: –KEY max mana. Gain 1d4 mana whenever you roll Initiative; this expires if unused at the end of combat.

boons.name: Sniper
boons.text: Advantage on attacks when no enemy is adjacent to you; disadvantage otherwise.

boons.name: Tough
boons.text: Whenever you gain temp HP, gain 5 more.

boons.name: Unflinching
boons.text: Your focus is unbroken even in the face of danger. Advantage on Concentration saves.

boons.name: Epic Criticals
boons.text: Whenever you roll for critical hit damage, you may replace one die with a d20.

boons.name: Epic Foresight
boons.text: Gain +5 to Initiative rolls and advantage on your first attack each encounter.

boons.name: Epic Knowledge
boons.text: (1/Safe Rest) You can call upon a moment of profound insight to gain hidden knowledge about a legendary being or object.

boons.name: Epic Mana
boons.text: Whenever you are healed, you may instead recover 1 mana for every 5 HP of healing.

boons.name: Epic Resistance
boons.text: (1/encounter) Whenever you would take damage or fail a save, you don’t.

boons.name: Epic Stamina
boons.text: Rolling 4 or higher on a Hit Die during a Field Rest heals 1 Wound.

stats.name: Strength
stats.text: Your raw physical power and resilience, endurance, and resistance to harm. Affects STR weapon damage, resistance to Wounds, HP recovery, Concentration, STR saves, carrying capacity, Grappling, and the Might skill.

stats.name: Dexterity
stats.text: Your agility, reflexes, and precision with blades or bows. Affects DEX weapon damage, Initiative, DEX saves, Grappling, and can contribute to Defense, as well as the Stealth and Finesse skills.

stats.name: Intelligence
stats.text: Your Intelligence reflects knowledge and reasoning across fields like the arcane, tactics, or street smarts. Affects languages, spellcasting, use of wands, spell scrolls, INT saves, as well as the Arcana, Examination, and Lore skills.

stats.name: Will
stats.text: Your force of personality, courage, and wisdom. Will shapes your interactions with both nature and society. Affects spellcasting and WIL saves, as well as the Insight, Influence, Naturecraft, and Perception skills.

skills.name: Arcana
skills.text: Understanding of magical phenomena, spells, and enchantments. With Arcana, you can identify magical effects, decipher arcane symbols, and discern the properties of magical items. It also grants insights into the abilities and weaknesses of magical beings like Aberrations, Elementals, and Oozes.

skills.name: Examination
skills.text: Aptitude for thorough analysis and deduction. Use Examination to diagnose injuries, determine causes of death, uncover clues, and unravel the workings of traps or mechanical devices. It also grants insights into the abilities and weaknesses of Constructs.

skills.name: Finesse
skills.text: The ability to use your hands and feet in careful ways. Use Finesse for activities such as picking locks, disarming traps, piloting vehicles, tinkering, card tricks, stealing or planting items, climbing a mossy wall, or any other task that requires precise, careful movement.

skills.name: Influence
skills.text: Your persuasiveness, charm, and ability to influence others through charisma or cunning. Use Influence to convince or deceive people, negotiate deals, build trust, win allies to your cause, or put on a captivating performance.

skills.name: Insight
skills.text:
Your ability to understand people and situations beyond the obvious. Use Insight to sense motives, detect lies, read hidden emotions, make sense of clues, and when faced with uncertainty—you can think ahead or just “get” what is happening. Insight can be used to retroactively change situations:
Player: “Oh no! I forgot to buy rope back in town!”
GM: “Give me an Insight check; maybe your hero would have thought about it…”

skills.name: Lore
skills.text: Understanding of the history of civilization, kingdoms, and religions. Use Lore to recall historical events and grasp the significance of cultural practices. It extends to knowledge of the abilities and behavior of Celestials, Dragons, Fey, Fiends, Giants, Humanoids, and Undead.

skills.name: Might
skills.text: Your ability to apply strength effectively. Use Might for lifting heavy objects, breaking through obstacles, climbing, swimming, jumping, or performing feats of strength.

skills.name: Naturecraft
skills.text: Your expertise in wilderness survival, navigation, tracking, and the handling of animals. Use Naturecraft to thrive in the wild, identify flora, fauna, and track creatures with precision. It encompasses knowledge of Beasts, Monstrosities, and Plants, providing insights into their behavior, habitats, and characteristics.

skills.name: Perception
skills.text: Your overall ability to notice subtle details in your surroundings. Use Perception to spot hidden objects, detect secret passages, sense subtle environmental changes, and sense when you’re being followed or observed. It encompasses your ability to pick up on non-obvious cues and hidden threats.

skills.name: Stealth
skills.text: Your proficiency in staying unseen and moving quietly. Use Stealth to hide, slip past guards, evade detection, and move without drawing attention.

rules.languagesText: All heroes speak Common by default. Each point of INT grants you an additional language known.
rules.levelUpText: The GM may allow you to gain a level (LVL) while Safe Resting after you complete an appropriately challenging quest or adventure. At level 1, this may be as simple as clearing some angry rats out of a basement or rescuing someone from the woods. Each subsequent level will generally take more effort (and therefore more time). When you gain a level:
levelUp: HP Increase. Roll your Hit Die with advantage and increase your max HP by that much (or you may take the average instead: Hit Die size: d4: +3 HP; d6: +4 HP; d8: +5 HP; d10: +7 HP; d12: +8 HP).
More Endurance. Your Hit Die max increases by 1 (it is typically equal to your level).
More Skilled. Gain 1 skill point. Additionally, to reflect your hero’s evolving expertise and priorities you may move 1 point from one skill to another (as long as the skill isn’t already negative).
Class Features. Gain new class features for your level. This may mean increasing your mana pool, new spells, or even selecting a subclass!

Other Adjustments. If any of your base stats increase, remember to adjust other elements of your character sheet as needed: skills change with their respective stats, as do damage, Initiative, Defense, mana, languages, etc.
rules.inventory:
Each hero has 10+STR inventory slots for carrying equipment and loot (held, worn, or in a pack).
• 1 slot can hold a 1-handed weapon, shield, worn armor, stack of javelins, 500 gp, or 2 potions.
• 2 slots can hold a 2-handed weapon, unworn armor, or similarly bulky items.
• Small, related items can be grouped into one slot for simplicity (e.g., Camping Supplies: soap, blanket, brush, rations).

On Ammunition. In most games, there’s no need to track ammo. If you have a quiver, you have enough arrows. Assume the hero collects fired arrows, crafts more, or buys them in town.

Alternatively, your GM may allow you to carry whatever you want without the bookkeeping, so long as you’re reasonable!
rules.defaults: Mark your HP, Hit Dice size (see your class), Hit Die amount (default: LVL), Defense (DEX+armor), Initiative (default: DEX), Size, Speed (default: 6), max Wounds (default: 6), and inventory slots (10+STR).
rules.startingGold: Heroes start at level 1 with the equipment listed for their class and background OR 50 gp to buy their starting equipment. If starting at a higher level, multiply that by your starting level.

equipmentRules.name: Equipment Proficiency
equipmentRules.text: Heroes can use any equipment they like; however, each class has a list of weapons and armor types they are most skilled with. Weapons used without proficiency cannot crit. Defending while wearing armor without proficiency costs 1 additional action.

equipmentRules.name: Swapping Equipment
equipmentRules.text: A hero can sheathe weapons or shields they are proficient with and equip a different one for free 1/round.

equipmentRules.name: Armor & Defense
equipmentRules.text: Defense represents your hero’s ability to dodge or block damage when you use the Defend reaction. While unarmored or wearing regular clothes, your Defense is equal to your **DEX**. Some items may grant additional Defense while equipped.

equipmentRules.name: Defend Yourself!
equipmentRules.text: If you’re standing right next to a baddie with an axe and you’re not doing anything to defend yourself, chances are, you’re going to get axed (see Defend on pg. 15 for more)!

equipmentRules.name: Deflect!
equipmentRules.text: An optional rule for additional defensive flexibility: instead of adding your shield’s Defense to your total as normal, you may reduce the damage of an attack by your shield’s Defense value for free (1/round).

equipmentRules.name: Remember!
equipmentRules.text: Only the Primary Die (the leftmost one) determines whether an attack crits. Every time you roll crit damage, roll the additional Vicious die as well!

equipmentRules.name: Dual Wielding
equipmentRules.text: Heroes may wield 2 Light weapons at the same time. While dual wielding, (1/round) you may gain advantage on an attack with those weapons. You may dual wield 1-handed weapons without the Light property if your STR is 3 or greater, or 1 weapon without the Light property if your STR is 2. If completely unarmed, fists/feet can be dual wielded if proficient in Unarmed Strikes.

equipmentRules.name: Dual wielding different weapons?
equipmentRules.text: Roll dice for both weapons and choose either result instead (the 1/round limit still applies). Attacking with advantage? Add an extra die for one of the weapons.

equipmentRules.name: Unarmed Strikes
equipmentRules.text: To attack with your bare hands or feet, roll 1d4+STR. Heroes not proficient in Unarmed Strikes cannot crit.

equipmentRules.name: Improvised Weapons
equipmentRules.text: Using an improvised weapon (e.g., a chair, a frying pan, a big rock), default to 1d4+STR or 1d6+STR. Your GM may allow you to use bigger dice or other properties if it makes sense. An improvised weapon may be likely to break after a few hits, though!

equipmentRules.name: Customizing Weapons
equipmentRules.text: Can you reflavor a staff as a greatclub? Sure! A sai instead of a dagger? Of course! Could you pay a blacksmith to make your 3d4 Greatmaul deal 2d6 or 1d12 damage instead? Since the dice all add up to 12, it won’t break the game; ask your GM! Can a blacksmith make your dagger deal that much damage? No, sorry!

equipmentRules.name: Be Warned!
equipmentRules.text: Denizens of the dark may not appreciate the light and may attack the light bearers first. Certain spells (e.g., Fire, Lightning, and Radiant) may cause flashes of light as well and draw unwanted attention!

equipmentRules.name: Equipment Availability
equipmentRules.text: Costs for mundane items typically range from a few silver pieces to a few gold pieces. If you can find an artisan, you can commission them to create something for you—basically anything you can think of that their level of technology could support. The more ornate, the higher the price. Commissioning a special item typically starts around 50 gp and only goes up from there. Smaller towns will have fewer items and artisans than larger cities.

equipmentRules.name: What About…?
equipmentRules.text: These are not ALL of the items available for purchase, merely a sampling. If you can think of it, you can likely buy it!

equipmentRules.name: Currency
equipmentRules.text: Currency is made up of silver (sp) and gold pieces (gp). 10 silver = 1 gold. 1 sp is roughly the cost of a humble meal; 1 gp, a sumptuous feast. Most small towns will have equipment and items worth 50 gp or less. You’ll need to adventure to larger towns or cities or find a traveling merchant to purchase more valuable pieces of equipment.

equipmentRules.name: Magical Items
equipmentRules.text: Though some magical items can be purchased, most cannot. Some special shops may have a very small selection of them to purchase, but more typically these powerful items are acquired through adventuring.

equipmentRules.name: Typical Costs of Magical Items
equipmentRules.text:
Uncommon: Typically found around levels 2–6, 50–500+ gp.
Rare: Typically found around levels 5–12, 500–5,000+ gp.
Very Rare: Typically found around levels 8–18, 5,000–500,000+ gp.
Legendary: Typically found around levels 15–20, 1,000,000+ gp or priceless.

equipmentRules.name: Extra Arms?!
equipmentRules.text: Yes, you can dual wield 2-handed weapons or wear more than 1 shield, or Grapple 2 different creatures while hitting them both at the same time! Or any number of creative things, provided you have the arms to perform the task.

equipmentRules.name: Spell Scrolls
equipmentRules.text:
Spell scrolls are single-use inscribed magical spells (see Magic on pg. 44 for more). Casting a spell with a spell scroll does not cost mana, nor does it require magical ability. Anyone who can read the scroll’s language can use it. Reading one aloud takes the same number of actions the spell normally takes and consumes the scroll.

A character must make a **DC 10 Arcana** check to cast it successfully if they don’t already know a spell from that school; on a failure, it is wasted.

equipmentRules.name: Wands
equipmentRules.text:
Like spell scrolls, these can be used to cast spells without consuming mana and do not require magical ability. Unlike spell scrolls, wands can be recharged and used again. Characters proficient with wands can use one from any spell school, spending only the normal amount of actions to cast the spell.

Characters not proficient with wands must make a **DC 10+spell Tier Arcana** check to successfully cast the spell. Success or failure, the charge is spent.

equipmentRules.name: Combat Items
equipmentRules.text: Create combat-related items with a drawback so there is a choice to be made. It can be a one-time-use item, something that damages the hero, or something that needs to be recharged to be used again. Alternatively, you can have it become friends with the party, like Lumina!

equipmentRules.name: Secret Spells
equipmentRules.text: These spells are either incredibly powerful and banned from common knowledge, or ancient and simply lost to the ravages of time. They may not be appropriate for heroes to wield freely but can make for excellent quest rewards when found on scrolls, imbued in wands, or taught by a rare NPC. The mere existence of these spells can drive entire storylines and enrich your game world.

equipmentRules.name: Lodging Boons
equipmentRules.text:
Spending extra gold on lavish accommodations can provide valuable temporary benefits. These perks might include quicker recovery, valuable contacts, additional resources, or unique opportunities. The specific benefits depend on the quality of the lodging and the amount spent. You can roll from the table, or award a Minor, Major, or even EPIC Boon based on how much the heroes pay and where they rest:
• **A Minor Boon:** Typically costs around 10 gp.
• **A Major Boon:** Typically costs around 100 gp.
• **An EPIC Boon:** Typically costs around 1,000 gp.
These Boons are temporary and last only until the heroes take another Safe Rest. Adjust the cost and impact to suit your campaign and the party’s level of wealth.

equipmentRules.name: Boons
equipmentRules.text: Boons can be a great quest reward from a powerful patron (e.g., an elf queen, hearing of a hero’s bravery, could bestow them with the Brave or Lionhearted Boon), a temporary buff (e.g., a tonic that gives Epic Speed for 1 hour), or you can allow players to take a Minor/Major Boon instead of a Secondary/Key stat increase.

magicRules.name: Schools of Magic
magicRules.text: There are 6 core schools of magic. Each school has its own basic spells called cantrips and 9 Tiers of progressively more powerful spells that can be unlocked as heroes level up. Heroes can cast any spell from the schools that they know within the Tiers they have unlocked. Spells deal the damage type that matches the school (unless otherwise stated).

magicRules.name: Mana
magicRules.text: Powerful Tiered spells require mana—a portion of the spellcaster’s life force—to fuel them. A spell’s mana cost is equal to its Tier. Heroes gain mana as they level up. Cantrips cost no mana.

magicRules.name: Half on Save
magicRules.text: Creatures who save take half as much damage and suffer no other effects. Remember, a hero’s save DC is typically 10+KEY.

magicRules.name: Fire Spells
magicRules.text: Deal high, consistent damage at long range. Some fire spells can inflict Smoldering and gain additional destructive effects against Smoldering enemies.

magicRules.name: Ice Spells
magicRules.text: Deal medium damage at long range, with a focus on controlling the battlefield and protecting the spellcaster. Some ice spells have additional effects against Hampered targets.

magicRules.name: Lightning Spells
magicRules.text: Deal very high damage at medium range with a focus on teleporting around the battlefield and taking advantage of creatures equipped with metal. However, some lightning spells may fail to find ground and damage the spellcaster instead.

magicRules.name: Necrotic Spells
magicRules.text: Summon horrible minions or manipulate and trap targets. Some risky necrotic spells prey upon damaged creatures, sapping their very life force—but frequently fail to distinguish between friend and foe.

magicRules.name: Radiant Spells
magicRules.text: Can obliterate the unholy, the fearful, and those who would dare harm you or your allies. Equally effective at a distance or in melee. Other spells can protect, mend Wounds, and even restore creatures back to life!

magicRules.name: Wind Spells
magicRules.text: Aid in moving friend and foe alike around the battlefield. They can also slice and cut through entire groups of foes and viciously deal extra damage on critical hits.

magicRules.name: Secret Spells
magicRules.text: Some spells (or even entire spell schools) have been hidden or lost through the ages. Whether they are too dangerous or for other reasons, adventurers can sometimes stumble upon new spells (or wrench them out of the undead hands of a defeated Lich).

magicRules.name: Upcasting
magicRules.text: Each additional mana you spend on a Tiered spell makes it stronger (up to the Tier that you have unlocked). For example, a character that has Tier 3 spells unlocked can upcast a Tier 1 or 2 spell at Tier 3 by spending 3 mana.

magicRules.name: Range and Reach
magicRules.text: As with weapons, spells with “Range” can target from a distance, but have disadvantage if ANY enemy is adjacent to you. Add 1 die of disadvantage to gain +2 Range (max +6). Spells with “Reach” can’t do this, but work normally in melee.

magicRules.name: Smoldering
magicRules.text: This condition does nothing on its own, though some spells and abilities have additional effects against Smoldering creatures, ending the condition.

magicRules.name: Hampered
magicRules.text: A creature with actions or movement reduced (e.g., Dazed, Slowed, Grappled, Restrained, Prone, Difficult Terrain).

magicRules.name: D66
magicRules.text: Roll 2d6. The leftmost die is the tens place, and the second is the ones (e.g., 4 and 5 deal 45 damage).

magicRules.name: Charged
magicRules.text: Whenever you take lightning damage, you are Charged for 1 minute (or until combat ends).

magicRules.name: D88
magicRules.text: Roll 2d8. The leftmost die is the tens place, and the second is the ones (e.g., 4 and 5 deal 45 damage).

magicRules.name: D44
magicRules.text: Roll 2d4. The leftmost die is the tens place, and the second is the ones (e.g., 3 and 2 deal 32 damage).

magicRules.name: D44 with Advantage
magicRules.text: Roll 3d4 and drop the lowest die. The leftmost die is the tens place, and the second is the ones (e.g., 2, 3, and 4 deals 34 damage).

magicRules.name: D66 with Advantage
magicRules.text: Roll 3d6 and drop the lowest die. The leftmost die is the tens place, and the second is the ones (e.g., 2, 3, and 4 deals 34 damage).

magicRules.name: Utility Spells
magicRules.text: These spells are **not** learned like other cantrips; instead some classes can choose from among these additional spells as they level up.

magicRules.name: Cast Spell
magicRules.text: Casting a spell requires 1 free hand (or a held spellcasting focus), the ability to speak, and may require mana as well. A spell’s mana cost is equal to its spell Tier; cantrips cost no mana. **Upcasting Spells.** Some spells have a greater effect for each additional mana spent (see Magic on pg. 44 for more).

magicRules.name: Concentration
magicRules.text: Some activities require Concentration to maintain. A character can only Concentrate on one activity at a time. Whenever a character is **crit** while concentrating, they must make a **DC 10 STR save** or Concentration is broken and the activity fails. Concentration automatically ends (and cannot be begun) when a character is at 0 HP or is Incapacitated.
